title: Revealjs: code block at the end of a callout lost its bottom spacing since 1.8.15
description:
In Revealjs, when a code block is the last element of a callout, it now sits against the bottom of the callout. With `appearance="simple"` and no title, the code block border touches the callout border.

Gap between the bottom of the code block and the bottom of the callout, measured with Chromium on the example below:

| Callout | 1.7.34 | main |
|---|---|---|
| Default, titled, ending with code | 12.03px | 8.33px |
| Simple, untitled, ending with code | 15.74px | 0.93px |

The 0.93px is only the 1px callout border. Callouts ending with a paragraph render the same in both versions.

#13024 is first released in 1.8.15, so I expect the change to start there. I only rendered with 1.7.34 and main, not with 1.8.14 or 1.8.15.

## Reproducible example

````markdown
---
title: Callout last child code
format: revealjs
---

## Titled ending with code

::: {.callout-note}
## Titled

Some text.

```python
x = 1
```
:::

## Simple untitled ending with code

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Some text.

```python
x = 1
```
:::
````

## What happens

Since #13024, the HTML postprocessor wraps code blocks in a `div.code-copy-outer-scaffold` for the copy button. Revealjs uses the same postprocessor with `copyCode: true`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/e63ace9e50f55dd3ab3152d068738ed44a0987d0/src/format/reveal/format-reveal.ts#L260

So the last child of `.callout-content` is now the scaffold div and not `div.sourceCode`. Two rules added in #11251 to handle a code block in last position no longer match.

For simple untitled callouts, #11251 added a margin below a last `div.sourceCode` so that the code border does not merge with the callout border. This rule never matches now, which is the visible part:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/e63ace9e50f55dd3ab3152d068738ed44a0987d0/src/resources/formats/revealjs/quarto.scss#L975-L977

For titled callouts, the last child gets `padding-bottom: 0.5rem` and no margin, except when it is a `div.sourceCode`, which keeps the `var(--r-block-margin)` margin. This exclusion was there to avoid the duplicated background color on a code block in last position. The scaffold is not excluded, so it gets the 8px padding instead of the 12px margin. This one is more cosmetic.

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/e63ace9e50f55dd3ab3152d068738ed44a0987d0/src/resources/formats/revealjs/quarto.scss#L919-L926

We could make both selectors also target `div.code-copy-outer-scaffold` when it is the last child.

Related: #13446 and #13238 are about the same scaffold change on HTML callouts, which use different rules in the Bootstrap stylesheets.

title: revealjs: the closed slide menu stays in the Tab order, so focus lands on a panel that is off screen
description:
### I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

### Bug description

When the slide menu is closed it is moved off screen (`transform: translateX(-300px)`), but it stays in the tab order. Once a deck has more slides than the menu's slide list can show, the list becomes a scroll container. Chrome (130 and later) then makes it keyboard-focusable, because it has no focusable children of its own. Pressing <kbd>Tab</kbd> past the menu button therefore lands on `div.slide-menu-panel`, a panel the reader cannot see. Its accessible name is the text of every slide title.

This is the "menu is navigable when closed" point raised in https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/14249#issuecomment-4106827108. The maintainers there asked for it as a separate issue with a check that is not manual; the Playwright check below needs no screen reader. It is separate from the missing name on the menu button itself (#14249, #14251), and from off-screen *slides* in the tab order (#14795).

### Steps to reproduce

A deck long enough for the menu's slide list to scroll. Forty slides is plenty at 1280×720:

````qmd
---
title: "Menu probe"
format: revealjs
---

## Slide 1

[link on slide 1](https://example.com/1)

## Slide 2

[link on slide 2](https://example.com/2)

<!-- ... repeat through slide 40 ... -->
````

1. `quarto render deck.qmd`
2. Open `deck.html` in Chrome without clicking anything.
3. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> a few times.

### Actual behavior

On slide 1 (Chromium 141, measured by pressing Tab and reading `document.activeElement`):

```
Tab 1 -> a "link on slide 1"
Tab 2 -> a "link on slide 2"           (off-screen slide, #14795)
Tab 3 -> a (menu button, no name)      (#14249)
Tab 4 -> div.slide-menu-panel          <- the closed menu, at x = -300
Tab 5 -> leaves the document
```

The panel is reached only while it scrolls (`scrollHeight` 1518 vs `clientHeight` 660 here). In a deck whose slide list fits, the same panel is skipped, which is why short test decks do not show this.

### Expected behavior

While the menu is closed, nothing inside it is in the tab order or exposed to assistive technology. Opening it (button, <kbd>M</kbd>) restores it, so keyboard selection and clicks keep working.

Marking the closed menu `inert` does exactly that. I checked it in the rendered deck by adding this to the bundled `quarto-menu.js`. The menu plugin dispatches only `menu-ready` and opens or closes the menu by toggling `active` on `.slide-menu`:

```js
document.addEventListener("menu-ready", function () {
  const menu = document.querySelector(".slide-menu");
  if (!menu) return;
  const update = function () {
    menu.toggleAttribute("inert", !menu.classList.contains("active"));
  };
  update();
  new MutationObserver(update).observe(menu, {
    attributes: true,
    attributeFilter: ["class"],
  });
});
```

With it, Tab goes from the menu button straight out of the document. <kbd>M</kbd> followed by arrow keys and <kbd>Enter</kbd> still opens the menu, moves to the chosen slide and closes the menu again. Clicking the button and then a slide does the same. `inert` comes back each time the menu closes.

It belongs in `quarto-menu.js` rather than `menu.js`, because `menu.js` is a single minified line. Any other change to it, such as #14251, would conflict.

I'd be glad to send this as a PR with a Playwright test in `revealjs.spec.ts` and a changelog entry.

### Your environment

- IDE: none (rendered from the command line)
- OS: Linux
- Browser: Chromium 141 (Playwright)

The `quarto-menu.js` on `main` (fb25b49) is unchanged, so this applies to main as well.

### Quarto check output

```
Quarto 1.10.19
[✓] Checking versions of quarto binary dependencies...
      Pandoc version 3.10.0: OK
      Dart Sass version 1.101.0: OK
      Deno version 2.7.14: OK
      Typst version 0.15.1: OK
[✓] Checking versions of quarto dependencies......OK
```

title: a11y: footnote, citation, and cross-reference popups do not close with Esc
description:
## I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

## Bug description

The hover popups for footnotes, citations, and cross-references do not close
when the user presses Esc. This is true when the popup opens from the
pointer and when it opens from keyboard focus. The user must move the pointer
or the focus away to close it. This fails
[WCAG 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#content-on-hover-or-focus)
(the "dismissible" part).

A related problem: a popup with links in it (for example, a section
cross-reference) stays open after focus leaves the popup. At narrow widths
the open popup can cover the next focused element completely. This fails
[WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#focus-not-obscured-minimum).

#6500 is about screen readers in these popups. This issue is only about Esc
and focus, and the fix below does not remove existing behavior.

### Cause

[`tippyHover()`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b09757661f578d2b5cb1c0847c7c62c56993928e/src/resources/formats/html/templates/quarto-html-after-body.ejs#L267-L301) creates the popups with tippy.js 6.3.7.
Tippy does not handle Esc. Its docs give
[`hideOnEsc`](https://atomiks.github.io/tippyjs/v6/plugins/#hideonesc) as
example code for a custom plugin, not as a built-in, and Quarto does not add it.

Tippy hides an interactive popup on blur of the trigger, but not when focus
moves into the popup
([`onBlurOrFocusOut`](https://github.com/atomiks/tippyjs/blob/0c886b47b1cabc652d15126a6b03cb6611948178/src/createTippy.ts#L561-L579)).
After that, nothing watches focus leaving the popup.

The [code-annotation popups](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b09757661f578d2b5cb1c0847c7c62c56993928e/src/resources/formats/html/templates/quarto-html-after-body.ejs#L602-L666) with
`code-annotations: hover` have the same Esc problem.

### Possible fix

Add a plugin to `tippyHover()` and to the `hover` code-annotation config:

```js
const hideOnEscAndFocusOut = {
  name: 'hideOnEscAndFocusOut',
  defaultValue: true,
  fn(instance) {
    function onKeyDown(event) {
      if (event.key !== 'Escape') return;
      if (instance.popper.contains(document.activeElement)) {
        // move focus back to the trigger without reopening the popup
        instance.disable();
        instance.reference.focus();
        instance.enable();
      } else {
        instance.hide();
      }
    }
    function onFocusOut(event) {
      const to = event.relatedTarget;
      if (to && to !== instance.reference && !instance.popper.contains(to)) {
        instance.hide();
      }
    }
    return {
      onShow() {
        document.addEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown);
        instance.popper.addEventListener('focusout', onFocusOut);
      },
      onHide() {
        document.removeEventListener('keydown', onKeyDown);
        instance.popper.removeEventListener('focusout', onFocusOut);
      },
    };
  },
};
// in tippyHover(): config.plugins = [hideOnEscAndFocusOut];
```

I tested this in Chrome on a patched copy of the rendered repro below. Esc
closes all four popup types, from hover and from focus. Esc inside the popup
returns focus to the trigger. Tab out of the popup closes it. Shift+Tab from
the popup back to the trigger keeps it open.

## Steps to reproduce

````qmd
---
title: "Popups and Esc"
references:
  - id: knuth1984
    type: book
    author:
      - family: Knuth
        given: Donald E.
    title: The TeXbook
    issued: 1984
---

## Popups

A footnote.[^1] A citation [@knuth1984]. A figure, @fig-square.

@sec-target has a link.

[Next link](https://example.com/after).

[^1]: The footnote text.

::: {#fig-square}

A figure caption.
:::

## Target section {#sec-target}

This paragraph has [a link inside the popup](https://example.com/inside).
````

1. Render the document and open it in a browser.
2. Tab to the footnote reference. The popup opens. Press Esc.
3. Do step 2 again for the citation, "Figure 1", and "Section 2". Do it again with the pointer over each one.
4. Make the window narrow (390px). Tab to "Section 2", then press Tab until focus is on "Next link".

## Actual behavior

- Steps 2 and 3: Esc does nothing. The popup stays open.
- Step 4: Focus goes through the two links in the popup, then to "Next link".
  The popup stays open and covers "Next link".

- Esc closes the popup. If focus is in the popup, focus goes back to the trigger.

title: Move the OJS runtime and its Observable forks from quarto-dev/quarto into quarto-cli
description:
Following the discussion in quarto-dev/quarto#1180, we'd like to move the OJS runtime and its vendored Observable forks from quarto-dev/quarto into this repo.

**What's there today:** quarto-dev/quarto's `packages/ojs/` holds:
- `quarto-ojs-runtime`, which builds `quarto-ojs-runtime{,.min}.js` with rollup;
- five git subtrees: `external-observablehq-runtime`, `external-observablehq-stdlib`, `external-observablehq-parser`, `external-d3-d3-require` and `external-asg017-unofficial-observablehq-compiler`. `packages/ojs/notes.md` has the `git subtree` commands.

The built bundle is copied by hand into `src/resources/formats/html/ojs/` here; the last two bumps were 3da4b18f and 0c76075e. Nothing in quarto-dev/quarto uses OJS: the code sits in its Yarn workspaces only so that the runtime can link the forks.

**Why move it:**
- None of the OJS tests are in quarto-dev/quarto, so any change there goes untested until someone copies the bundle over here and runs the Playwright specs in `tests/docs/playwright/ojs/`.
- The original reason to keep it outside, that quarto-cli had no Node toolchain, no longer applies now that quarto-cli builds Node subprojects such as `src/webui/quarto-preview`.
- quarto-dev/quarto is switching from Yarn 1 to npm. The frozen subtrees' old build devDependencies (e.g. rollup 3 next to `rollup-plugin-terser` 7, mocha 9) would fail npm's peer checks, and they bring dev-only Snyk advisories.

**Proposed plan:**
1. Copy `packages/ojs/` to a location here, e.g. `src/resources/formats/html/ojs/runtime-src/` or a top-level `packages/ojs/`. Use `git subtree` or a plain copy, preserving history if we want it.
2. Add a build script that regenerates the two bundle files, and ideally a CI check that the committed bundle matches the source.
3. Bring along quarto-dev/quarto#1180's tooling update: rollup 4, `@rollup/plugin-terser`, commonjs 29 with `strictRequires: false`, node-resolve 16, and mime 4. With it, the runtime's build is clean under npm, and quarto-cli's 9 OJS Playwright specs pass. The PR description lists every bundle diff. The visible ones: `FileAttachment(…).mimeType` for `.js` becomes `text/javascript`, and mime 4 has a newer type table.
4. Once it lands here, delete `packages/ojs/` from quarto-dev/quarto. That repo's #1180 will become the deletion PR.

**Things to know:**
- Keep `@observablehq/inputs` on 0.10. Version 0.11 renames the form class (`__ns__` → `inputs-3a86ea`), which would break Shiny's button styling.
- Don't copy `packages/ojs/quarto-ojs-runtime/assets/quarto.css`; this repo's `quarto-ojs.css` is ahead of it.
- Rebuilding from current source also ships everything since the last bump (2024-02): acorn 8.17, the `debugger` removal, inspector 5.0.1 and Inputs 0.10.6.

title: Relative image paths resolve against the wrong directory in og:image and listing feeds for pages in subdirectories
description:
With a website project like

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
project:
  type: website

website:
  site-url: https://example.com
  image: site.png
  open-graph: true
```

and these two pages in subdirectories

```markdown
<!-- blog/index.qmd -->
---
title: "Blog"
---
```

```markdown
<!-- news/index.qmd, with news/thumb.png next to it -->
---
title: "News"
image: thumb.png
listing:
  feed: true
---
```

the rendered output points to files that don't exist:

- `blog/index.html` gets `og:image` set to `https://example.com/blog/site.png`, while `site.png` is at the project root
- `news/index.xml` gets the feed image `https://example.com/thumb.png`, while `thumb.png` is in `news/`

In both cases `og:image:width`/`og:image:height` and the feed `<width>`/`<height>` are missing too, as the image size is read from the wrong path. Pages at the project root are not affected, as both bases are the same there.

I can reproduce with 1.10.19 and current main.

Social metadata resolves any relative image path against the document. This includes the `website.image` fallback, which comes from `_quarto.yml`

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/53fda8160f1bc05cebbed182977a0aebae5de3aa/src/project/types/website/website-meta.ts#L181-L186

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/53fda8160f1bc05cebbed182977a0aebae5de3aa/src/project/types/website/website-meta.ts#L406-L422

The listing feed does the opposite and resolves everything against the project root, including the `image` of the listing page

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/53fda8160f1bc05cebbed182977a0aebae5de3aa/src/project/types/website/listing/website-listing-feed.ts#L169-L181

The docs say a page `image` is document relative, or project relative with a leading `/` (https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-tools.html#preview-images). They don't say anything about `website.image`, but as a default site image for every page it can only work if it is project relative. Same for `open-graph: image:` and `twitter-card: image:` set under `website:` in `_quarto.yml`, which are also resolved against each document today.

We could resolve each image against the base of the file it is written in:

- `website.image`, and `open-graph`/`twitter-card` `image` in `_quarto.yml`: project relative
- page `image`, and `open-graph`/`twitter-card` `image` in the page front matter: document relative
- listing `feed: image:`: project relative, as today and like `feed: xml-stylesheet:` next to it. Its schema description and the docs don't say what it is relative to, so this should be documented.

Paths starting with `/` and full URLs would keep working the same.

## Workaround

A leading `/` makes the path project relative, and it resolves the same way in both places:

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
website:
  image: /site.png
```

```yaml
# news/index.qmd
image: /news/thumb.png
```

Related: #5389 (which added the `website.image` fallback), #12016 and #12014 (`image-width`/`image-height` lost for `open-graph`/`twitter-card` images).

title: Revealjs callout with an id renders the id twice
description:
In revealjs, a callout with an id gets that id on two nested divs.

```markdown
---
format: revealjs
---

## Slide

::: {#my-id .callout-note title="Titled"}
Body.
:::
```

renders

```html
<div id="my-id" title="Titled">
<div id="my-id" class="callout callout-note callout-titled callout-style-default">
```

Duplicate ids are invalid HTML, `getElementById()` only finds the outer div, and a CSS `#my-id` rule applies to both. This happens for titled and untitled callouts, and for cross-referenceable ones (`#tip-xref`) too. HTML format is not affected, there the id is only on the `.callout` div. EPUB uses the same renderer as revealjs and has the same duplicate.

I can reproduce with 1.4.549, 1.9.38 and current main. 

The revealjs/epub renderer puts the identifier on the `.callout` div

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/2377f54c75d270ee5bce9af914ab8218b84110e7/src/resources/filters/customnodes/callout.lua#L190

and then wraps it in a div carrying the full original attributes, identifier included, whenever there is an id, a class or an attribute left

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/2377f54c75d270ee5bce9af914ab8218b84110e7/src/resources/filters/customnodes/callout.lua#L191-L197

The wrapper was added in 1.4 for #5208 and #6853, so that extra classes like `.fragment` are not lost. At that time the inner div did not get the id. The xref callouts support later changed the inner div to use the identifier, and the wrapper kept it as well.

We could keep the id on the `.callout` div only, like HTML does, and keep the wrapper only for the remaining classes and attributes.

## Workaround

For a callout that is not cross-referenced, put the id on a div around the callout:

```markdown
:::: {#my-id}
::: {.callout-note title="Titled"}
Body.
:::
::::
```

There is no workaround for cross-referenceable callouts, as the `#tip-` id needs to be on the callout itself.

title: revealjs: screen readers hear a Mermaid diagram's CSS, and not an image's fig-alt
description:
- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of Quarto CLI
- [x] formatted my issue following the Bug Reports guide

### Bug description

In revealjs presentations, what screen readers are told when a slide is entered (reveal.js's `.aria-status` live region) goes wrong for two of Quarto's own features:

1. **A Mermaid diagram is announced with its CSS.** Mermaid puts a `<style>` in the SVG it draws, and the bundled reveal.js reads it as text. Entering a slide with a three-node flowchart announces nearly 10,000 characters of CSS (`#mermaid-1{font-family:"trebuchet ms",verdana,arial,sans-serif;…`) before the node labels.
2. **`fig-alt` is not announced.** reveal.js 5.1.0, which Quarto bundles, reads no alt text, so entering a slide with an image announces only its caption.

Both come from `getStatusText()`, the function in the bundled reveal.js that builds these announcements. #15019 is about the same announcements, but these are separate problems with a separate fix, and #15020 does not change them. This is also not #3873, where `fig-alt` is not applied to a Mermaid diagram at all: here the image has its alt text, and the announcement leaves it out.

### Steps to reproduce

````qmd
---
title: "Diagrams"
format: revealjs
---

## Mermaid

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[Start] --> B[Middle] --> C[End]
```

## Graphviz

```{dot}
digraph G { Start -> End }
```

## Image

![A caption]({{< placeholder 200 100 >}}){fig-alt="A grey rectangle"}
````

Render it, open the presentation and step through it with →. To see the announcements without a screen reader, paste this into the browser console on the title slide first:

```js
new MutationObserver( records => records.forEach( r => r.addedNodes.forEach( n => console.log( JSON.stringify( n.textContent ) ) ) ) )
  .observe( document.querySelector( '.reveal .aria-status' ), { childList: true } );
```

### Actual behavior

Pressing → from the title slide:

| → | Announced |
|---|---|
| 1, to Mermaid | `Mermaid`, then 9,882 characters of CSS (`#mermaid-1{font-family:"trebuchet ms",verdana,arial,sans-serif;…`), then `Start Middle End` |
| 2, to Graphviz | `Graphviz G Start Start End End Start->End` |
| 3, to Image | `Image A caption` |

Each is announced twice, as #15019 reports, so the Mermaid slide reads its CSS twice.

The Graphviz slide is there for comparison. Its SVG has no `<style>`, so no CSS is announced, but each node is announced twice, from its `<title>` and its label.

### Expected behavior

- Mermaid: the slide title and the node labels, without the CSS.
- Image: the slide title, the alt text and the caption.

### Your environment

- Quarto 1.10.19, and main at a57cc76
- Chromium 141 on Linux

### Quarto check output

Not included: the problem is in the bundled reveal.js that runs in the browser, and it is the same on 1.10.19 and on main.

### Fix

- **The CSS** is reported upstream with a fix in hakimel/reveal.js#3948. The same change has reveal.js announce an element with `role="img"` by its name instead of the text inside it. Today maidr's charts, for example, are announced by their tick labels.
- **The alt text** is announced by reveal.js since 6.0.0.

With a build of reveal.js master (e240e175) that has the change from hakimel/reveal.js#3948, swapped into the rendered presentation:

| Slide | Announced |
|---|---|
| Mermaid | `Mermaid. Start. Middle. End.` |
| Graphviz | `Graphviz. G Start Start End End Start->End.` |
| Image | `Image. A grey rectangle. A caption.` |

Quarto bundles 5.1.0, so it gets these from a reveal.js release that has them, or by carrying them in the bundled 5.1.0, as #15020 proposes for #15019.

Graphviz is covered by neither. It gives every node and edge a `<title>`, and the upstream change leaves `<title>` alone: a `<title>` can be the only name a graphic has, and for an unlabelled Graphviz edge it is the only text.

title: Dashboard: HTML output containing "bsli" is mistaken for bslib output and pulled out of its card
description:
### I have: - [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues - [x] installed the latest version of Quarto CLI (1.10.19; also reproduced on the 1.11.5 pre-release) - [x] formatted my issue following the Bug Reports guide ### Bug description In `format: dashboard`, an HTML cell output whose text contains the letters `bsli` anywhere is moved out of its card and placed in front of it. Examples of such outputs are `IPython.display.HTML` and `htmltools::HTML`. If that output was all the cell showed, which is the default because dashboards don't echo code, the card is dropped as well, title included. Text and Markdown outputs are not affected. The dashboard filter treats a `.cell-output-display` holding a single HTML raw block as bslib output when the block's text matches `'bslib-'`: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/a57cc76458d91a0577c162a474929119e6b663ba/src/resources/filters/quarto-post/dashboard.lua#L273 In a Lua pattern, `-` is a quantifier: zero or more of the preceding character, as few as possible. So `'bslib-'` means "`bsli` followed by zero or more `b`": | Text | `match('bslib-')` | `match('bslib%-')` | |---|---|---| | `bslib-card` | match | match | | `bslib` | match | no match | | `subslide` | match | no match | | `

bsli

` | match | no match | So besides `bslib-`, it matches `bslib` with no hyphen, words such as "subslide" and "subslice", and any chance occurrence of `bsli` in minified script or base64 data. I hit this in py-maidr, which writes the maidr.js bundle and a small script into the cell output. A reference to bslib's JavaScript namespace (`bslib`, with no hyphen) pulled the chart out of its card. maidr.js and py-maidr now build that name from parts at runtime, and maidr.js fails its build if `bsli` appears anywhere in a bundle. Related: #14719 is about the same lift (`bslibRawOutputs` in `dashboard.lua`) when the output really is bslib: there the cell's options are not applied to the lifted output. This issue is about output that is wrongly treated as bslib in the first place. ### Steps to reproduce ````qmd --- title: "Dashboard" format: dashboard --- ```{python} #| title: First card from IPython.display import HTML HTML("

A subslide of the deck

") ``` ```{python} #| title: Second card HTML("

Plain text

") ``` ```` The same happens with knitr, for example with `htmltools::HTML("

A subslide of the deck

")` in an `{r}` chunk. ### Actual behavior The page has one card, "Second card". `

A subslide of the deck

` sits directly inside `.quarto-dashboard-content`, above the layout grid, and "First card" and its title are gone. Output from 1.11.5. 1.10.19 is identical apart from the `id`, `tabindex` and `role` attributes on the first div: ```html

A subslide of the deck

``` With `echo: true`, "First card" survives and holds only the code, and the output is placed in front of it. ### Expected behavior Two cards, "First card" and "Second card", each holding its own output. Only output containing the literal `bslib-`, the prefix of bslib's classes and attributes, should be lifted. That is evidently what the pattern means. Escaping the hyphen fixes it: `text:match('bslib%-')`, or a plain find, `text:find('bslib-', 1, true)`. I patched `'bslib%-'` into 1.11.5's `share/filters/main.lua`: - Both the Jupyter reproduction and the knitr reproduction render both cards with their outputs. - A dashboard whose cell outputs `bslib::value_box(title = "Value", value = 42)` renders byte-identical HTML with and without the patch, so real bslib output is still lifted. A few anchored patterns elsewhere also end in an unescaped `-`. One example is `c:match("^column-")` in `quarto-pre/parsefiguredivs.lua` (line 339), which matches any class starting with `colum`, while `layout/columns.lua` escapes the same pattern as `^column%-`. I haven't checked whether any of them has a visible effect. `'bslib-'` is the unanchored one, which is why it fires on text anywhere in the output. ### Your environment - IDE: none (command line) - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS - Jupyter reproduction: Python 3.9.25 in a virtual environment with ipykernel 6.31.0, passed as `QUARTO_PYTHON` - knitr reproduction: R 4.3.3, knitr 1.52, htmltools 0.5.9 - value box check: bslib 0.6.1 ### Quarto check output From 1.11.5, the latest pre-release, run with the same `QUARTO_PYTHON`. I also reproduced the bug on 1.10.19, the latest release, which uses Pandoc 3.10. ``` Quarto 1.11.5 [✓] Checking environment information... Quarto cache location: /root/.cache/quarto [✓] Checking versions of quarto binary dependencies... title: revealjs: screen readers hear incremental content before it is revealed, and each slide twice
description:
- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of Quarto CLI
- [x] formatted my issue following the Bug Reports guide

### Bug description

In revealjs presentations, what screen readers are told (reveal.js's `.aria-status` live region) has two problems:

1. **Content is announced before it is revealed.** Entering a slide with an incremental list announces every bullet, including the ones not shown yet. The same goes for `. . .` pauses and other fragments. A screen reader user hears the whole slide before it is revealed, then each bullet again as it appears.
2. **Slides are announced twice.** Quarto sets `history: true` by default, and each slide made from a heading has an id. With both, reveal.js handles its own `hashchange` by navigating to the slide again, which announces it a second time. With `fragment-in-url: true`, each Space also announces the new bullet three times and then the whole slide again.

With a screen reader, stepping through a slide with Space then sounds like the content already on it being read again before each new bullet.

Both come from reveal.js, and I reported them upstream with a proposed fix: hakimel/reveal.js#3945. The same code is in reveal.js 5.1.0, which Quarto bundles, and in 6.0.2 and master.

### Steps to reproduce

````qmd
---
title: "Incremental test"
format:
  revealjs:
    incremental: true
---

## Slide A

- First point
- Second point
- Third point

## Slide B

- Alpha
- Beta
````

Render it, open the presentation and step through it with Space. To see the announcements without a screen reader, paste this into the browser console on the title slide first:

```js
new MutationObserver( records => records.forEach( r => r.addedNodes.forEach( n => console.log( JSON.stringify( n.textContent ) ) ) ) )
  .observe( document.querySelector( '.reveal .aria-status' ), { childList: true } );
```

### Actual behavior

Pressing Space from the title slide:

| Space | Announced |
|---|---|
| 1, to Slide A | `Slide A First point Second point Third point`, twice |
| 2 | `First point` |
| 3 | `Second point` |
| 4 | `Third point` |
| 5, to Slide B | `Slide B Alpha Beta`, twice |

Opening the presentation announces `Incremental test` twice as well.

With `fragment-in-url: true`, Space 2 announces `First point` three times and then `Slide A First point Second point Third point`, and so on for every bullet.

### Expected behavior

Each announcement once: `Slide A` when the slide is entered, then only the bullet each Space reveals.

### Your environment

- Quarto 1.10.19, and main at a57cc76
- Chromium 141 on Linux

### Quarto check output

Not included: the problem is in the bundled reveal.js that runs in the browser, and it is the same on 1.10.19 and on main.

### Fix

I checked the upstream change in a rendered Quarto presentation by swapping in a reveal.js build that has it: `Slide A` is announced once when the slide is entered, then only the new bullet on each Space, with `fragment-in-url` on or off. Quarto bundles 5.1.0 and the move to 6.x is a separate upgrade, so Quarto could carry the change until then, as #15010 did with the `inert` fix from reveal.js 6.0.2.

In the meantime, `history: false` stops the repeated announcements. The URL still follows the slides, but the browser's Back button no longer steps through them. Nothing stops content from being announced before it is revealed.

title: a11y: notebook preview "Back to Article" link has no href in website projects
description:
## I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

## Bug description

On a notebook preview page (`*-preview.html`) rendered in a website project, the "Back to Article" control is an `<a>` without an `href`. Without `href` it has no link role, is not in the Tab order, and cannot be activated from the keyboard. Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot go back to the article.

The template writes the element with only an `onclick` handler:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/e63ace9e50f55dd3ab3152d068738ed44a0987d0/src/resources/formats/html/embed/template.html#L121

The same markup is served on quarto.org: https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/penguins-preview.html has `<a onclick="window.quartoBackToArticle(); return false;" class="btn btn-primary quarto-back-link">` with no `href`.

In a standalone (single-file) render the output has `href=""` on the same element, so something adds an empty `href` there. I don't know yet what does it, and why it doesn't happen in a website render.

The `backHref` metadata is already used by `quartoBackToArticle()` as a fallback when there is no history to go back to, so the destination is known at render time when it is set.

## Steps to reproduce

Website project with `_quarto.yml`, `index.qmd` and an executed `notebook.ipynb`.

`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website
```

`index.qmd`:

````qmd
---
title: Home
---

{{< embed notebook.ipynb#answer >}}
````

```bash
quarto render
grep -o '<a [^>]*quarto-back-link[^>]*>' _site/notebook-preview.html
```

Output:

```html
<a onclick="window.quartoBackToArticle(); return false;" class="btn btn-primary quarto-back-link">
```

Rendering the same `index.qmd` as a single file (outside a project) gives `... class="btn btn-primary quarto-back-link" href="">`.

## Possible fix

We could add an `href` to the template (e.g. `$nbMeta.backHref$` when set) and keep the `onclick`, which already returns `false` so the history-based back behavior is unchanged. This needs checking against axe, and against the case where `backHref` is not set.

Found while testing #14972. Related to #14968.

title: revealjs: the keyboard focus drops to the page body when the slide that has it becomes inert
description:
### I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

### Bug description

Since #15010, every slide but the current one and the stack holding it is `inert`. When the keyboard focus is on the slide being left, for example on a link the reader tabbed to, making that slide inert takes the focus away and the browser puts it on `<body>`. `focusout` fires on the link with no `relatedTarget`, and no `focusin` follows: nothing in the presentation has the focus any more.

Before #15010 the focus stayed on the link, which was then off screen (#14795). #15010 fixed that. What is left is that the focus needs somewhere to go when its slide becomes inert.

For screen reader users, where it goes decides whether the arrow keys work. reveal.js gives the deck `role="application"`. While the focus is on something in the deck, a link on a slide for example, NVDA and JAWS pass the arrow keys on to reveal.js. On `<body>` they are in browse mode, where <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> read the page instead of changing slides. So a screen reader user who has tabbed to a link can change slides once, and then has to press <kbd>Tab</kbd> again before the arrow keys change slides again.

Anything that puts the focus on a slide is affected the same way. maidr, which makes charts accessible to blind and low-vision readers, moves the focus to the chart's slide when the reader leaves a chart with <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd>. The next <kbd>→</kbd> drops that focus to `<body>`.

reveal.js 6.0.2, whose rule #15010 mirrors, does the same. In a page with only reveal.js 6.0.2 and three slides like the ones below, <kbd>→</kbd> leaves the focus on `<body>` too. With NVDA and with JAWS on Windows, the arrow keys then stop changing slides until <kbd>Tab</kbd> is pressed again.

### Steps to reproduce

````qmd
---
title: "Focus probe"
format: revealjs
---

## Slide 1

[link on slide 1](https://example.com/1)

## Slide 2

Text only.

## Slide 3

[link on slide 3](https://example.com/3)
````

1. Render it with Quarto 1.11.6 (or main) and open it in Chrome.
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd>. The focus is on "link on slide 1".
3. Press <kbd>→</kbd>.
4. Look at `document.activeElement` in the console.

### Actual behavior

`document.activeElement` after each key, in Chromium 141 (Playwright):

| Key | 1.11.6, and main at b09757661 | 1.10.19 |
|---|---|---|
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | "link on slide 1" | "link on slide 1" |
| <kbd>→</kbd> | `<body>` | "link on slide 1", now off screen (#14795) |
| <kbd>Tab</kbd> | the slide menu button | "link on slide 3", off screen (#14795) |

### Expected behavior

The focus stays in the presentation, where screen readers keep passing the arrow keys on. Moving it to the deck before the slide that has it is made inert does that. In `updateInertSlides()` in `support.js`:

```js
function updateInertSlides(deck) {
  const allowAllSlides = deck.isOverview() || deck.isScrollView() || deck.isPrintView();
  const currentSlide = deck.getCurrentSlide();
  const revealElement = deck.getRevealElement();
  revealElement.querySelectorAll('.slides section').forEach((slide) => {
    const inert = !allowAllSlides && slide !== currentSlide && !slide.contains(currentSlide);
    // Making the slide that holds the focus inert would drop it to the body.
    if (inert && slide.contains(document.activeElement)) {
      if (!revealElement.hasAttribute('tabindex')) revealElement.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
      revealElement.focus({ preventScroll: true });
    }
    slide.toggleAttribute('inert', inert);
  });
}
```

I checked it in the rendered deck above. With it, <kbd>→</kbd> moves the focus from the link to the deck: `focusout` names the deck as its `relatedTarget`, and `focusin` follows on the deck. The next <kbd>Tab</kbd> goes to the menu button, as it does now. `tabindex="-1"` keeps the deck out of the Tab order, and Chrome draws its focus ring around the deck. A plugin that focuses something on the new slide in its own `slidechanged` handler still can, since this one runs first, in the capture phase.

I'd be glad to send this as a PR, with a test next to #15010's in `revealjs.spec.ts` and a changelog entry.

### Your environment

- IDE: none (rendered from the command line)
- OS: Linux
- Browser: Chromium 141 (Playwright)
- Screen readers: NVDA and JAWS on Windows, for the reveal.js 6.0.2 check

### Quarto check output

```
Quarto 1.11.6
[✓] Checking versions of quarto binary dependencies...
      Pandoc version 3.10.0: OK
      Dart Sass version 1.101.0: OK
      Deno version 2.7.14: OK
      Typst version 0.15.1: OK
[✓] Checking versions of quarto dependencies......OK
```

<details>
<summary>AI-assisted issue</summary>

- **Codebase grounding**: Local clones of Quarto main and reveal.js, Quarto 1.10.19 and 1.11.6, and the deck above rendered with each and measured in Chromium with Playwright.
- **Screen reader check**: I checked the reveal.js 6.0.2 page with NVDA and JAWS on Windows, as described above.
- **Human review**: I reviewed this report and approved it.

</details>

title: Wrong category link when post is contained in multiple listings
description:
### I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

### Bug description

Category links go to the wrong location when there are multiple listings.

We have this issue on https://topos.institute

Minimal reproduction: https://github.com/ToposInstitute/quarto-category-link-bug-repro

### Steps to reproduce

```
git clone https://github.com/ToposInstitute/quarto-category-link-bug-repro.git
cd quarto-category-link-bug-repro
quarto preview
```

- http://localhost:5142/
- Go to "Post one"
- Click on the "Alpha" category

### Actual behavior

Goes to http://localhost:5142/index.html#category=alpha which does not filter by category

### Expected behavior

Goes to http://localhost:5142/blog/index.html#category=alpha


LLM diagnosis: 

> ## Root cause
> 
> `src/resources/formats/html/quarto.js` defines `findNearestParentListing`:
> 
> ```js
> const findNearestParentListing = (href, listingHrefs) => {
>   if (!href || !listingHrefs) return undefined;
>   const relativeParts = href.substring(1).split("/");
>   while (relativeParts.length > 0) {
>     const path = relativeParts.join("/");           // "blog/post-one/", "blog/post-one", "blog", ""
>     for (const listingHref of listingHrefs) {
>       if (listingHref.startsWith(path)) return listingHref; // listingHref is "/blog/index.html"
>     }
>     relativeParts.pop();
>   }
>   return undefined;
> };
> ```
> 
> `listingHrefs` entries always begin with `/` (e.g. `/blog/index.html`,
> `/index.html`); `path` is built without a leading slash. So
> `"/blog/index.html".startsWith("blog/post-one/")` is `false`, and so are all
> later iterations *until* `path === ""`, which matches every listing. The
> function therefore returns `listingHrefs[0]` — whatever happens to be first.
> 
> In this repro `/index.html` ends up first in `listings.json`, so all post
> categories link to the home page.
> 
> ## Suggested fix
> 
> Compare against a leading slash, or use a "longest-directory-prefix" match:
> 
> ```js
> const findNearestParentListing = (href, listingHrefs) => {
>   if (!href || !listingHrefs?.length) return undefined;
>   const postDir = href.replace(/[^/]+$/, "");        // "/blog/post-one/"
>   let best, bestLen = -1;
>   for (const listingHref of listingHrefs) {
>     const listingDir = listingHref.replace(/[^/]+$/, ""); // "/blog/"
>     if (postDir.startsWith(listingDir) && listingDir.length > bestLen) {
>       best = listingHref;
>       bestLen = listingDir.length;
>     }
>   }
>   return best;
> };
> ```
>

title: Render crashes when a proof, remark or solution block has an id that is not a cross-reference id
description:
### I have

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

### Bug description

A `proof`, `remark` or `solution` block that carries an id crashes the render when the id is not one of the cross-reference prefixes (`prf-`, `rem-`, `sol-`).
It fails in HTML and in Typst.
A theorem block such as `::: {#my-thm .theorem}` with the same kind of id renders fine.

The error depends on the id:

- With a hyphen, such as `#my-proof`, `refType` returns `my`, which is not a cross-reference category, so `parseblockreftargets.lua` indexes a nil category.
- Without a hyphen, such as `#myproof`, the block reaches `add_crossref` with no category, and `crossref/index.lua` uses a nil table index.

I came across this while working on something else, and narrowed it down to the small example below.

### Steps to reproduce

````qmd
---
title: "Proof with an id"
format: html
---

::: {#my-proof .proof}
A proof with an id.
:::
````

Then run `quarto render`.
Replacing `#my-proof` with `#myproof` gives the second error.

### Actual behavior

With `#my-proof`:

```text
.../resources/filters/./quarto-pre/parseblockreftargets.lua:44: attempt to index a nil value (field '?')
```

With `#myproof`:

```text
.../resources/filters/./crossref/index.lua:48: table index is nil
```

### Expected behavior

The block renders as an unnumbered proof that keeps its id, as it does without an id.

### Your environment

- IDE: none, command line.
- OS: macOS 27.0.

title: Website category with a short backtick run before a longer one renders as broken code
description:
### I have - [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues - [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest) - [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html) ### Bug description A website category that holds a backtick run followed later by a longer run renders as a broken code span, with Quarto's internal markup showing on the page. A category whose longest run comes first renders fine. Quarto passes each category to Pandoc as inline code with the `{=pandoc-native}` raw attribute, so that Markdown does not touch it. `pandocNativeStr` in `src/core/pandoc/codegen.ts` makes that wrapper one backtick longer than the first run in the text, not the longest. A later, longer run then closes the inline code early. The Reveal.js script paths and the Reveal.js URL go through the same function, but I have not tried those. A roborev code review flagged this while I was working on something else, and I confirmed it with the smaller example below. description:
_Edited: based on @cderv comment and with additional examples_ ## Considering the below example for Quarto `fig-alt` attribute: ```md ## Section ![Caption for Quarto Logo](https://quarto.org/quarto.png){fig-alt="Quarto Logo"} ``` |`quarto pandoc index.qmd --from markdown --to docx -o index.docx` | `quarto render index.qmd --to docx`| |:-:|:-:| | | | ## Using Pandoc markup, caption + alt text ends up in Word alt text (so no real issues): ```md ## Section ![Caption for Quarto Logo](https://quarto.org/quarto.png "Quarto Logo") ``` |`quarto pandoc index.qmd --from markdown --to docx -o index.docx` | `quarto render index.qmd --to docx`| |:-:|:-:| | | | ## Using computations: ````md ## Section ```{r} #| label: fig-plot #| fig-cap: "A caption for a plot" #| fig-alt: "An alt text for a plot" plot(1) ``` ```` |`quarto pandoc index.qmd --from markdown --to docx -o index.docx` | `quarto render index.qmd --to docx`| |:-:|:-:| | Obviously not working | | Note that computation with figures will generate the following markdown (for both `knitr`/`Jupyter`): ```md ![A caption for a plot](index_files/figure-docx/fig-plot-output-1.png){#fig-plot fig-alt='An alt text for a plot'} ``` --- The initial question also mentioned `pdf`, but I don't even know how to show alternative text in PDF. --- ### Discussed in https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/5511
Originally posted by **IZE85** May 12, 2023 In MS Word, one is able to "add alternative text to a shape, picture, chart, SmartArt graphic, or other object to help people with visual disabilities." When I add alternative text to a figure via "fig-alt" it gets exported via HTML. Unfortunately, when knitting to formats like Word or PDF, my fig-alt text is saved/deposited somewhere, if I'm correct. At least, for MS Word, I cannot see the alternative text in the "alternative text" field, MS Word provides for figures. My question: Is it possible for the fig-alt text to find its way into the MS Word Alternative text field and have something similar for PDFs? Thank you in advance! Ad alternative text: "Alt text helps people with visual disabilities understand pictures and other graphical content. When someone using a screen reader comes across a picture in a document, they will hear the alt text describing the picture; without alt text, they will only know they've reached a picture without knowing what the picture shows." Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/add-alternative-text-to-a-shape-picture-chart-smartart-graphic-or-other-object-44989b2a-903c-4d9a-b742-6a75b451c669

title: [Accessibility] fig-alt does not work for mermaid
description:
Currently, `fig-alt` does not work for mermaid diagram. However, there seems a workaround. Mermaid has their own [accessibility options](https://mermaid.js.org/config/accessibility.html).

@cscheid -- We may want to bind `fig-cap` to `accTitle` and `fig-alt` to `accDescr`. Other additional accessibility fixes that I am not mentioning here need to be taken care of on mermaid side.

## Reprex

````

---
title: "Untitled"
format: html

title: DOCX: an image with empty `fig-alt` is not marked as decorative in Word
description:
With #15077, an explicit empty `fig-alt` in `docx` output gives an empty Word picture description, instead of using the caption.

```markdown
![A caption](image.png){fig-alt=""}
```

In `document.xml`, the picture gets `<wp:docPr descr="" ...>`.

This is the intent for a decorative image, and it matches HTML where we write `alt=""`. However, Word does not consider an empty description as decorative. Word has a separate **Mark as decorative** setting for this, as described in Microsoft's guidance:
https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/accessibility/office-accessibility/everything-you-need-to-know-to-write-effective-alt-text

Pandoc's DOCX writer does not write this setting, so for now authors need to mark the image as decorative in Word after export.

We could map an explicit empty `fig-alt` to Word's decorative setting. This needs some checking first:

- Which markup Word writes in `document.xml` when an image is marked as decorative (saving a document from Word would tell us)
- How Word's accessibility checker reports an image with an empty description today, and with the decorative setting
- Whether this belongs in Pandoc's DOCX writer for an image with empty alt, or in Quarto's `docx` post-processing

Where to look for the markup: `wp:docPr` accepts an `extLst` child for extensions ([docPr definition](https://schemas.liquid-technologies.com/officeopenxml/2006/docpr.html)), and Microsoft documents its Office drawing extensions to OOXML in [MS-ODRAWXML](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/). I did not find the decorative setting described there yet, so a document saved from Word is probably the quickest way to confirm it.

Discussed in https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/pull/15077#issuecomment-6220106807

Related: #14348, #14142

title: Shortcodes inside math are not resolved when they are the only shortcodes in the document
description:
### I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of Quarto CLI
- [x] formatted my issue following the Bug Reports guide

### Bug description

Follow-up to #14255 / #14279. Since 1.10, shortcodes inside math are resolved, but only if the document also contains a shortcode somewhere outside math. If the math shortcodes are the only ones, they stay in the output verbatim.

Cause, as far as I can tell: the shortcode filter only runs when `compute_flags()` sets `flags.has_shortcodes`, and `compute_flags()` (`src/resources/filters/normalize/flags.lua`) checks `Shortcode`, `Code`, `RawInline`, `RawBlock`, `CodeBlock`, `Link`, `Image` and attributes, but not `Math`. The test added in #14279 (`shortcode-math.qmd`) also has `Plain: {{< meta five >}}` outside math, which sets the flag and hides this case.

For LaTeX output this breaks compilation as soon as the shortcode takes TeX arguments (e.g. an extension shortcode like `{{< qty 3 \meter >}}` in an equation gives `\meter ->\ERROR`).

### Steps to reproduce

````qmd
---
title: Shortcode only in math
format: html
five: 5
---

Inline: $5 + {{< meta five >}}$

Display: $$5 + {{< meta five >}}$$
````

### Actual behavior

Both formulas contain the literal `{{< meta five >}}` (HTML: `5 + {{< meta five >}}`).

Adding any shortcode outside math (e.g. `Text {{< meta five >}}`) makes both formulas render correctly.

### Expected behavior

`5 + 5` in both formulas, independent of other shortcodes in the document.

### Your environment

- OS: macOS 26 (arm64)

title: a11y: website sidebar toggles and page links are too small for WCAG 2.5.8
description:
## I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

## Bug description

In the website sidebar, two kinds of targets fail
[WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#target-size-minimum):

- **Section toggles** (the chevron next to a section that has an `href`) are
  20.4 × 18 px. The toggle shares an edge with the section link, so the 24px
  spacing exception does not apply. The link and the toggle do different
  things, so the "equivalent" exception does not apply either.
- **Page links** are 17 px tall, and their centres are 23.8 px apart. The
  24px circles of two adjacent links overlap by 0.2 px. This is a fail by a
  very small margin.

Sections without an `href` (one button for the label and the chevron) pass on
spacing.

On quarto.org the values are almost the same: toggles 20.4 × 18.8 px, links
17.0 px tall at a 23.8 px pitch (Safari 27 and Chrome, at 320px and 1280px).

Related: #14826 made the toggles into buttons. Open PR #14867 deletes the
toggle `:focus-visible` rule, which is next to the lines below. The fix below
does not touch that rule.

### Cause

In [`quarto-nav.scss`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/45cc5991938018ca5e69a92aa73d4daa504e05f1/src/resources/projects/website/navigation/quarto-nav.scss#L356-L360),
`.sidebar-item` has `line-height: 1rem`, `margin-top: 0.4rem`, and
`margin-bottom: 0.2em`. These give the 17px link height and the 23.8px pitch.

The toggle has [`padding: 0`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/45cc5991938018ca5e69a92aa73d4daa504e05f1/src/resources/projects/website/navigation/quarto-nav.scss#L382-L390)
and a [`0.7rem` icon](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/45cc5991938018ca5e69a92aa73d4daa504e05f1/src/resources/projects/website/navigation/quarto-nav.scss#L420-L424),
so it is only as big as the icon and its `ms-2` margin.

### Possible fix

```scss
// Make the toggle a 24px target without a change to the row height:
// the negative margins cancel the extra height.
.sidebar-item .sidebar-item-toggle:not(.sidebar-item-text) {
  min-width: 24px;
  min-height: 24px;
  margin-block: -3px;
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  align-self: flex-start;
}

.sidebar-item {
  margin-top: 0.45rem; // was 0.4rem: link pitch goes from 23.8px to 24.6px
}
```

I injected this CSS into the rendered repro below and measured it with
Chrome Headless at 320px and 1280px:

- All targets pass at both widths.
- Toggles are 24 × 24 px. Page links are 24.6 px apart.
- The rows with a toggle keep their height. The chevron stays on the first
  line of a section name that wraps.
- The list gets 0.8 px longer per item.
- Toggles are 3.6 px wider, so a long section name can wrap one word earlier.

The `:not(.sidebar-item-text)` excludes the full-width button of a section
without an `href`. That button already passes.

## Steps to reproduce

`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website
website:
  sidebar:
    contents:
      - text: "Home"
        href: index.qmd
      - section: "Guide"
        href: index.qmd
        contents:
          - text: "page-a"
            href: index.qmd
          - text: "page-b"
            href: index.qmd
      - section: "Reference"
        contents:
          - text: "page-c"
            href: index.qmd
          - text: "page-d"
            href: index.qmd
```

`index.qmd`:

````qmd
---
title: Home
---

Text.
````

1. Render the project and open `_site/index.html`.
2. In the browser console, run
   `document.querySelector('#quarto-sidebar .sidebar-item-toggle').getBoundingClientRect()`.
3. Do the same for the "page-a" and "page-b" links.

## Actual behavior

| Target | Size (px) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| "Guide" toggle | 20.4 × 18.0 | Fail: 24px circle overlaps the "Guide" link |
| page-a, page-b, page-c, page-d links | 205 × 17.0, 23.8 px apart | Fail: circles overlap by 0.2 px |
| "Reference" button (no `href`) | 213 × 18.0 | Pass on spacing |

The values are the same at 320px and 1280px.

## Expected behavior

Each target is at least 24 × 24 px, or it has the spacing that
[2.5.8](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#target-size-minimum) requires.

## Your environment

- IDE: none (rendered from the terminal)

title: Missing hyphenation package not installed when babel loads the language from its .ini file (babeloptions: provide=*)
description:
With `babeloptions: provide=*`, babel sets up the document language from its `.ini` file. When the hyphenation patterns for this language are not installed, the PDF is produced with English hyphenation, and Quarto does not install the missing package.

With TinyTeX without **hyphen-spanish** installed:

````markdown
---
format: pdf
lang: es
babeloptions: provide=*
---

Hola, esto es una prueba de separación silábica.
````

`quarto render` gives `Output created` with no warning. The log only has an Info line:

```
Package babel Info: Hyphen rules for 'spanish' set to \l@english
(babel)             (\language0). Reported on input line ...
```

The same happens with `\babelprovide[import]{<lang>}` in a raw LaTeX header. Without `provide=*`, babel uses the `.ldf` files, which warn about missing patterns, and this case is already handled.

The detection of missing hyphenation packages follows `check_babel()` in **tinytex**, plus a check for `\l@nil` that does not match here:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/cbb00db1c49123e7e68fb6e22c70a769d403ee17/src/command/render/latexmk/parse-error.ts#L286-L309

Detecting this from the log is not obvious, as the same Info line is also there for valid dialects, and the language name is a babel locale name and not a `language.dat` name. Details and the possible detection are in rstudio/tinytex#519. We'll work on it in **tinytex** first, and then port the same detection here like for #15035.

title: `fig-alt` lost for Mermaid and Graphviz diagrams in LaTeX output
description:
With #15077, `fig-alt` on Mermaid and Graphviz diagrams is now honored in HTML, revealjs, DOCX and Typst output. It is still lost in LaTeX output (`pdf`, `beamer`), while a regular figure in the same document gets its alt text.

````markdown
---
format:
  pdf:
    keep-tex: true
---

```{dot}
//| label: fig-dot
//| fig-cap: "A Graphviz diagram"
//| fig-alt: "Graphviz alternative text"
digraph G { A -> B }
```

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-mermaid
%%| fig-cap: "A Mermaid diagram"
%%| fig-alt: "Mermaid alternative text"
flowchart LR
  A --> B
```

![An image](image.png){#fig-image fig-alt="Image alternative text"}
````

The `.tex` file has no `alt` key for the two diagrams:

```latex
\includegraphics[width=5.5in,height=3.5in]{repro_files/figure-latex/dot-figure-1.png}
\includegraphics[width=2.13in,height=0.73in]{repro_files/figure-latex/mermaid-figure-1.png}
\pandocbounded{\includegraphics[keepaspectratio,alt={Image alternative text}]{image.png}}
```

Same result with `beamer` (the example from #9003), and for diagrams without label or without caption.

The diagram handlers write `fig-alt` on the generated image. For Typst, it is converted to `alt` on the image here:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/0e28ab3aedd44be2c95433a29a6aff9250fbcc75/src/resources/filters/quarto-post/typst.lua#L218-L223

It seems nothing does the same for LaTeX on this path. Regular captioned figures work because they go through the figure handling, but the diagram output doesn't benefit from it even with a caption.

This is close to #14315 (`fig-alt` lost for LaTeX non-float images), but not the same case: a captioned diagram also loses it, while a captioned image does not. We could check whether one LaTeX-side conversion fixes both.

Part of #14348.

title: Install dehyph-exptl for pinned German patterns and follow the tinytex hyphenation map
description:
Follow-up to #15027 / #15029. The table of hyphenation names in `parse-error.ts` is a hand-written copy of the one in **tinytex** and it is already behind.

tinytex now generates this table from the `execute AddHyphen` lines of `texlive.tlpdb` (rstudio/tinytex#517, follow-up to rstudio/tinytex#516). The generated table has 41 entries, the 37 we have plus 4 that map to `dehyph-exptl`: `german-x-latest`, `ngerman-x-latest`, `german-x-2024-02-28` and `ngerman-x-2024-02-28`.

## What is missing here

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/db1d1c70ab25e12dd2d651fadb69c15c4d774eb8/src/command/render/latexmk/parse-error.ts#L161-L201

1. `dehyph-exptl` can't be expressed. The values are suffixes and the package is always built as `hyphen-${name}`, then checked against `^hyphen-[a-z0-9-]+$`.

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/db1d1c70ab25e12dd2d651fadb69c15c4d774eb8/src/command/render/latexmk/parse-error.ts#L205-L232

So a log with `You haven't defined the language 'ngerman-x-latest' yet` gives the non-existent `hyphen-ngerman-x-latest`.

2. `findMissingHyphenationFiles` only returns one package. The warning regex has no `g` flag, so with several `Package babel Warning: No hyphenation patterns were preloaded` messages only the first language is handled.

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/db1d1c70ab25e12dd2d651fadb69c15c4d774eb8/src/command/render/latexmk/parse-error.ts#L260-L281

3. A language name with a space, like ``the language `German (new orthography)' `` in a `(babel)` line, doesn't match `` language [`'](\S+)[`'] ``. tinytex keeps the first word (`german`) for those.

4. polyglossia is not handled in `src/command/render/latexmk/` (tinytex handles `Package polyglossia Warning: No hyphenation patterns were loaded for ...`).

The `chinese` skip list and the `\l@nil` fallback exist here only, and tinytex doesn't have them.

## Plan

The tinytex daily build now exports the map as `hyphen.json` inside the `regex.tar.gz` of the `daily` release of `rstudio/tinytex-releases`, next to `regex.json` (once rstudio/tinytex#517 is merged):

```json
{
  "ngerman": "hyphen-german",
  "ngerman-x-latest": "dehyph-exptl"
}
```

Values are full package names, only exceptions to `hyphen-<name>` are listed.

Other ways to share the data that I looked at:

- Our own generator in Deno against `texlive.tlpdb`: no dependency on tinytex, but two generators and a new workflow to maintain for the same data.
- Fetching `R/hyphen.R` from the tinytex repository at build time: it needs parsing R syntax from TypeScript and adds a network dependency to the build.
- Keeping two copies by hand: this is what we have now, and the 4 `dehyph-exptl` entries show that it drifts.

Reusing `regex.tar.gz` fits the existing setup: `verify-tinytex-patterns.yml` already downloads it daily from the `daily` release of `rstudio/tinytex-releases`. That workflow only opens or comments on an issue (label `tinytex-patterns`), it never opens a PR, so the table would still be updated by hand after the report. We could also extend it to open a PR with the new table, but the table in `parse-error.ts` is TypeScript with comments and the test file has its own copy, so I would start with the report only.

Two things to keep in mind: `hyphen.json` only exists in the release once rstudio/tinytex#517 is merged and the daily build ran, and a change of its format would break the comparison step (which today only reads `regex.json` with `jq`).

We could:

- Switch `kHyphenationPackageNames` to full package names, add the 4 `dehyph-exptl` entries, and validate the language name (`^[a-z0-9-]+$`) instead of the resulting package.
- Extend `verify-tinytex-patterns.yml` to also compare `hyphen.json`, so the existing `tinytex-patterns` issue tells us when the map changes. Its `jq` steps only read `regex.json` today. This keeps the table bundled, with no network access at build or run time.
- Update the copy of the table in `tests/unit/latexmk/parse-error.test.ts` and `dev-docs/tinytex-pattern-maintenance.md`.
- Look at points 2 to 4 above separately, if they turn out to be real.

## Still to check

Everything above comes from reading the code, nothing was run yet.

- [ ] Reproduce points 2 to 4 with small log samples in a Deno unit test (`tests/unit/latexmk/parse-error.test.ts`), and confirm which ones are real with logs produced by babel/polyglossia.
- [ ] Point 1: confirm that `findMissingHyphenationPackages` returns `hyphen-ngerman-x-latest` for `You haven't defined the language 'ngerman-x-latest' yet`.
- [ ] Check that `hyphen.json` is really in the `daily` release asset once rstudio/tinytex#517 is merged and the daily build ran, and that the existing `regex.tar.gz` download step still works with the extra file.
- [ ] Check if the `chinese` / `chinese-hans` skip list is still needed (#10291), and if `pinyin` -> `hyphen-chinese` in the generated map interacts with it.
- [ ] Decide if polyglossia support belongs here or if it is not needed for Quarto's PDF output.

Related: rstudio/tinytex#515, #10291.

title: Website `og:image` and `twitter:image` use a data URI prefixed with `site-url`, ignoring `website.image`
description:
<!-- markdownlint-disable MD041 MD034 -- the template has no top heading, and bare permalinks render as code snippets on GitHub -->
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD026 -- heading text is fixed by the quarto-cli bug template -->
### I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

### Bug description

In a website project, Quarto uses the first image on a page for `og:image` and `twitter:image` when the page doesn't set `image`.
If that first image is a data URI, Quarto still picks it, and prefixes it with `site-url`.
The tag ends up as `https://example.com/data:image/png;base64,...`, which no social platform can fetch.
The site-wide `website.image` would have been a valid fallback, but the data URI wins over it.

Authors can hit this without writing an image at all.
When the `author` block has an `orcid`, Quarto renders the ORCID badge as a 16 by 16 PNG data URI, and that badge is the first image on the page.

Two steps in the code lead to this.
`findPreviewImgEl` returns the first image whose `src` starts with `data:`, in the same pass that looks for feature, cover and thumbnail file names:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b86f98d382940bef6c65f37ea0bdfba844f19b6d/src/project/types/website/util/discover-meta.ts#L65-L75

`imageMetadata` then treats the value as a relative path and joins it to `site-url`, because `isAbsoluteRef` only recognises `http://` and `https://`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b86f98d382940bef6c65f37ea0bdfba844f19b6d/src/project/types/website/website-meta.ts#L427-L468

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b86f98d382940bef6c65f37ea0bdfba844f19b6d/src/core/http.ts#L24-L26

On `main`, the render now fails instead.
Since #15050, `imageSize` checks every path on disk rather than only `.png` paths, so the data URI is passed to `existsSync` as a file name.
On macOS, this stops the render with `File name too long (os error 63)`.

### Steps to reproduce

`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: "OG repro"
  site-url: https://example.com
  image: site.png
  open-graph: true
  twitter-card: true
```

`index.qmd`:

````qmd
---
title: "Home"
author:
  - name: Jane Doe
    orcid: 0000-0002-0000-0000
---

Some text.
````

`other.qmd`:

````qmd
---
title: "Other"
---

Some text.
````

Add any PNG as `site.png` at the project root, then run `quarto render`.

### Actual behavior

With 1.9.38, 1.10.18, 1.10.19 and 1.11.6, `_site/index.html` has:

```html
<meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABAAAAAQ...">
<meta name="twitter:image" content="https://example.com/data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABAAAAAQ...">
```

`_site/other.html` correctly has `https://example.com/site.png`, with its width and height.

With `main` at b86f98d382940bef6c65f37ea0bdfba844f19b6d, the render fails on `index.qmd`:

```text
ERROR: File name too long (os error 63): stat '<project>/data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo...'

Stack trace:
    at Object.statSync (ext:deno_fs/30_fs.js:432:3)
    at existsSync (https://jsr.io/@std/fs/1.0.16/exists.ts:268:23)
    at imageSize (src/core/image.ts:16:9)
    at imageMetadata (src/project/types/website/website-meta.ts:458:18)
    at resolveImageMetadata (src/project/types/website/website-meta.ts:358:21)
```

### Expected behavior

Quarto skips data URIs when it looks for a preview image, because social platforms can't fetch them.
`index.html` then falls back to `website.image`, as `other.html` does.

If a data URI does end up in `image`, Quarto leaves it as it is: no `site-url` prefix, and no attempt to read its size from disk.

- OS: macOS 27.0 (Apple Silicon).
