title: Typst: brand Google font dropped from font list when another document in the same directory was rendered first
description:
When two documents in the same directory (or the same project) use different `brand` Google fonts with Typst, the second render can silently drop its brand font from the `font:` list and fall back to the next font. Deleting `.quarto/typst/available-fonts.json` makes it work again.

This is a regression from 1.9. Running the example below (render `first.qmd` then `second.qmd`) with different versions:

| Version | `font:` in `second.typ` | Font in `second.pdf` |
|---|---|---|
| 1.9.38 | `("Barrio", "Libertinus Serif")` | Barrio |
| 1.10.9 | `("Barrio", "Libertinus Serif")` | Barrio |
| 1.10.10 | `("Libertinus Serif",)` | Libertinus Serif |
| 1.10.18 | `("Libertinus Serif",)` | Libertinus Serif |

1.10.10 is the first build with #14580.

## Reproducible example

Two files in an empty directory.

`first.qmd`

````markdown
---
format: typst
brand:
  typography:
    fonts:
      - family: Tiny5
        source: google
    base: Tiny5
---

First document.
````

`second.qmd`

````markdown
---
format:
  typst:
    keep-typ: true
brand:
  typography:
    fonts:
      - family: Barrio
        source: google
    base: Barrio, Libertinus Serif
---

Second document.
````

Rendering `second.qmd` alone gives the expected font:

```bash
quarto render second.qmd
grep "font: (" second.typ
#   font: ("Barrio", "Libertinus Serif"),
pdffonts second.pdf
# PZZALO+Barrio-Regular   CID TrueType ...
```

Rendering `first.qmd` before it drops Barrio:

```bash
rm -rf .quarto second.typ second.pdf
quarto render first.qmd
quarto render second.qmd
grep "font: (" second.typ
#   font: ("Libertinus Serif",),
pdffonts second.pdf
# IEFFFX+LibertinusSerif-Regular-Identity-H   CID Type 0C ...
```

Barrio was downloaded correctly to `.quarto/typst/fonts/` alongside Tiny5, it is only missing from the font list. Removing `.quarto/typst/available-fonts.json` and rendering `second.qmd` again gives back `("Barrio", "Libertinus Serif")`.

## What happens

Since #14580, we filter unavailable fonts from Typst font-family lists using the output of `typst fonts`. That list is cached on disk in `.quarto/typst/available-fonts.json`, keyed on a hash of the font paths only:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/62eb719b95f060cd5f8d0d94a1e858e5d1c0de5b/src/core/typst.ts#L54-L79

Brand Google fonts are always downloaded into the same `.quarto/typst/fonts` directory, so the font paths are identical for every document sharing that `.quarto`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/62eb719b95f060cd5f8d0d94a1e858e5d1c0de5b/src/command/render/pandoc.ts#L1617-L1621

The first render caches a font list that only knows about Tiny5. The second render downloads Barrio into the same directory, gets a cache hit on the same key, and Barrio is then filtered out as unavailable:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/62eb719b95f060cd5f8d0d94a1e858e5d1c0de5b/src/resources/filters/modules/typst_css.lua#L697-L702

The same happens in a project when the brand font changes after a first Typst render. In a project with `_brand.yml` using `base: Tiny5, Libertinus Serif`, rendering once and then switching to `base: Barrio, Libertinus Serif` gives `font: ("Libertinus Serif",)` on the second render (also with 1.11.5). If none of the listed fonts is in the stale list, the filter keeps the full list, which is why a single-font `base: Barrio` does not show the problem.

This was found through a CI failure on `docs/smoke-all/typst/brand-yaml/typography/font-list.qmd`, which fails when `title-inherit-base-family.qmd` from the same directory is rendered before it in the same test bucket.

We could include the content of the font directories (file names and modification times) in the cache key, so that a new download invalidates the cached list.

title: Footnotes in title or author trigger heading shift in PDF/Typst with number-sections
description:

- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

### Bug description

With `number-sections: true` and PDF (or Typst) output, an inline footnote in `title`, `subtitle` or `author` makes Quarto apply `shift-heading-level-by: -1`, even though the document has level-1 headings. As a result:

- the first level-1 heading becomes the document title
- other level-1 headings become plain text
- level-2 headings are numbered as level 1 (e.g., "1 First Hypothesis" instead of "1.1")

Setting `shift-heading-level-by: 0` explicitly restores the expected output. Word and HTML are not affected.


### Steps to reproduce

`````md
````qmd

---
title: "Header test"
author: "Jane Doe^[A footnote in the author field.]"
number-sections: true
format: pdf
# uncomment the next line to fix the headers

---

# Introduction

Rendering this file to PDF shows three problems.
First, "Introduction" replaces "Header test" as the title of the document,
because it is the first level-1 header.

## First Hypothesis

Second, this level-2 header is numbered "1", as if it were a level-1 header.

# Conclusion

Third, this level-1 header renders as plain text.

Removing the footnote, removing `number-sections`, or uncommenting
`shift-heading-level-by: 0` fixes all three.

````
`````

### Actual behavior

The PDF's title is "Introduction", and "First Hypothesis" is numbered 1. The same happens with `format: typst`.

### Expected behavior

The title is "Journals: A Mock Paper" (with its footnote), "Introduction" is section 1, and "First Hypothesis" is 1.1.

title: Incremental renders rewrite sitemap.xml lossily: undated entries are dropped or inherit a neighbouring date
description:
## Environment

- Quarto 1.10.18 (macOS 26, arm64)
- Defect is in the website project type's sitemap reader (`readSitemap()` in the bundled quarto.js, used by `updateSitemap()` on incremental renders).

## Description

The sitemap spec makes `<lastmod>` optional, but `readSitemap()` only retains an `<url>` entry when **both** `loc` and `lastmod` have been seen — and it never resets `loc`/`lastmod` between entries. On an incremental render, Quarto re-reads an existing `_site/sitemap.xml` and rewrites it, so:

1. **Entries dropped:** every `<url>` without `<lastmod>` that appears *before* the first dated entry is silently removed.
2. **Dates inherited:** every undated entry *after* a dated one is retained, but inherits the preceding entry's `<lastmod>` — a date that does not belong to it.

## Minimal reproduction (standalone project, verified with Quarto)

```sh
mkdir sitemap-repro && cd sitemap-repro
printf '%s\n' 'project:
  type: website
  output-dir: _site

website:
  site-url: https://example.com' > _quarto.yml
for p in index about x y z; do printf '%s\n' '---' "title: $p" '---' '' "Page $p." > "$p.qmd"; done
quarto render
```

Overwrite `_site/sitemap.xml` with this mixed dated/undated inventory:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/index.html</loc>
  </url>
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/about.html</loc>
  </url>
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/x.html</loc>
    <lastmod>2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z</lastmod>
  </url>
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/y.html</loc>
  </url>
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/z.html</loc>
  </url>
</urlset>
```

Then trigger one incremental render of a single page:

```sh
touch y.qmd && quarto render y.qmd
```

Actual resulting `_site/sitemap.xml`:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/x.html</loc>
    <lastmod>2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z</lastmod>
  </url>
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/y.html</loc>
    <lastmod>2026-10-03T15:02:41.874Z</lastmod>
  </url>
  <url>
    <loc>https://example.com/z.html</loc>
    <lastmod>2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z</lastmod>
  </url>
</urlset>
```

The undated `index.html` and `about.html` entries were dropped (they precede the first dated entry), and `z.html` inherited `x.html`'s `2024-01-01` date. `y.html` received its own fresh date only because it was the page rendered in that run.

## Expected

The full URL inventory is preserved; `lastmod` is optional per the sitemap spec, so undated entries survive as undated. At minimum, parser state must be reset per `<url>` so no date is inherited.

## Analysis

A faithful model of the bundled `readSitemap()` callback semantics (`text`: `loc`/`lastmod` ← text; `end_element`: push on `loc && lastmod`; **no reset** between entries) reproduces the behaviour above exactly, and also predicts what we observed on a real site: a committed sitemap with 37 `<loc>` entries, only 2 dated, was rewritten by an incremental render to **11 entries, 9 of which carried an inherited (wrong) date** — matching the reader model for that input. The two defects are visible in both the isolated reproduction and the real site's incremental render.

## Workaround

Our workaround rebuilds the sitemap after each render from the rendered pages' canonical tags, omitting `lastmod`. This restores the complete inventory independently of the sitemap Quarto has rewritten.

## Suggested fix

Reset `loc`/`lastmod` at the start of each `<url>` element, and retain entries with `loc` regardless of `lastmod`.

title: Bump bundled Pandoc to include texmath spacing fix (Typst math regression in Pandoc 3.10/texmath 0.13.1.x)
description:
### Summary

Quarto currently bundles a Pandoc version that appears affected by a Typst math spacing regression from texmath 0.13.1.x, fixed in texmath 0.13.2.1 (first fixed Pandoc release appears to be 3.10.2).

### Repro

```bash
echo '$[x]^T \in$' | quarto pandoc -f markdown -t typst
```

### Observed

On affected Pandoc versions, output loses spacing between `T` and `in` in Typst math (rendering as if tokens are joined).

### Expected

A space should be preserved between `T` and `in` in generated Typst math.

### Notes

- This reproduces on Pandoc 3.10 (and likely 3.9.0.1–3.10.1).
- Pandoc 3.8.3 bundled in Quarto 1.9.x is OK.
- Pandoc 3.10.2+ appears fixed (includes texmath 0.13.2.1 fix: “Typst writer: Fix spacing after escaped expressions”).

Would you consider bumping Quarto’s bundled Pandoc to a fixed version?

title: quarto render fails when a parent directory contains an unreadable folder (project detection treats it as existing)
description:
**Background:** when a document's folder has no `_quarto.yml`, Quarto walks up the parent folders running each project type's detect rules (e.g. Hugo: `config/_default/config.toml` plus `content`). The first match becomes the project root.

**Bug:** detection uses `safeExistsSync` (`src/core/path.ts`), which calls `@std/fs` `existsSync`. On `PermissionDenied`, with `--allow-read` granted, that returns `true` ("exists but can't be read"). So any parent folder containing an **unreadable** `config/` and a `content/` folder counts as a Hugo project, even though `config/_default/config.toml` can't be shown to exist. Quarto then treats that ancestor as the project, walks it, and the render fails on the unreadable folder.

**Repro** (macOS, Quarto 1.7.31 and 1.10.18):
```bash
mkdir -p x/config/_default x/content x/a/b
printf -- '---\ntitle: t\n---\nhello\n' > x/a/b/doc.qmd
chmod 000 x/config
(cd x/a/b && quarto render doc.qmd)
```
```
ERROR: PermissionDenied: Permission denied (os error 13): readdir '.../x/config'    # 1.10.18
ERROR: WalkError: Permission denied (os error 13): readdir '.../x/config'           # 1.7.31
```
No HTML is written. `quarto inspect doc.qmd` shows the same misdetection: it creates `x/.quarto`. Expected: render `doc.qmd` as a single file in `x/a/b`.
- With `config/` readable, the render succeeds.
- Adding a `_quarto.yml` to `x/a/b` also makes it succeed.

If the misdetected root is also not writable, as on some network or object-store mounts, the render fails earlier, with `ERROR: attempt to write a readonly database` from `ProjectCacheImpl.init`.

**Suggested fix:** in project detection, only count a detect file that is confirmed to exist and be readable, e.g. `existsSync(path, { isReadable: true })`, or treat `PermissionDenied` as "not found" in `safeExistsSync`. Stopping the upward walk at a filesystem boundary would also prevent this class of problem.

**Workaround:** put a minimal `_quarto.yml` (`project: { type: default }`) in the document's folder.

quarto create-project test-engine

project:

title: Document how to avoid an empty `<h2>` on revealjs slides without a visible title
description:
The revealjs docs show slides with no title, for example `## {background-color="aquamarine"}` in [Slide Backgrounds Without a Title](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/#slide-backgrounds-without-a-title) and `## {auto-animate=true}` in [Auto Animate](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/advanced.html#auto-animate). Each of these slides renders an empty `<h2>`. Screen reader users who move by headings land on a heading with no name, and axe reports `empty-heading`.

Authors can avoid the empty `<h2>` and still show no title. Put the title in a span with the `.visually-hidden` class:

```markdown
## [Aquamarine slide]{.visually-hidden} {background-color="aquamarine"}
```

In Quarto 1.11.4, the title does not show on the slide, but Chrome's accessibility tree has `heading "Aquamarine slide" [level=2]`. The slide menu also lists "Aquamarine slide", not the first words of the slide text. The class works in revealjs, because Quarto defines its own `.visually-hidden` ([`_quarto-rules.scss` L12-L22](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/abc6a78ed68f9e8bc9d54e27851093bd687a1cb7/src/resources/formats/html/_quarto-rules.scss#L12-L22)). The revealjs theme includes that file ([`format-reveal-theme.ts` L177](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/abc6a78ed68f9e8bc9d54e27851093bd687a1cb7/src/format/reveal/format-reveal-theme.ts#L177)).

quarto.org does not document this pattern, and there is a trap: `## Title {.visually-hidden}` hides **the whole slide**. In revealjs, Pandoc moves heading classes to the `<section>`.

**Suggestion:** In [Slide Backgrounds Without a Title](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/#slide-backgrounds-without-a-title), show the `.visually-hidden` span as the way to have no visible title, and warn about the class on the heading. [Auto Animate](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/advanced.html#auto-animate) could link to it.

AI helped with this investigation. The work was grounded in a local clone of quarto-cli, as "Using AI tools to investigate" in CONTRIBUTING.md describes.

title: a11y: the collapsed "On this page" toggle cannot be used with a keyboard
description:
## I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

## Bug description

Content in the right column (for example a `.column-page-right` figure) can overlap the margin TOC. In that case, Quarto collapses the TOC into an "On this page" toggle. Keyboard users cannot open this toggle.

1. **The toggle is not keyboard operable** ([2.1.1 Keyboard](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#keyboard)). The toggle title is a `<div>` with only an `onclick` handler. It has no `tabindex`. In 60 Tab presses, focus did not go to it. `focus()` on it did not work. Enter did not open it. A mouse click opened it.
2. **Hidden TOC links stay in the tab order** ([2.4.7 Focus Visible](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#focus-visible)). The original TOC links get `opacity: 0` but stay in the DOM. In the repro, 5 of 60 Tab presses stopped on these invisible links. The page showed no focus indicator.
3. **The toggle has no role or state** ([4.1.2 Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#name-role-value)). The accessibility tree shows only the text "On this page". There is no button role and no `aria-expanded`.

Secondary problems:

- The toggle is outside any landmark. axe-core 4.10.3 reports `region` (Best Practice) on `.quarto-sidebar-toggle-title`.
- The toggle contents are a clone of `nav#TOC`. This duplicates the `#TOC` id and the "On this page" navigation landmark.

**Cause:** `manageSidebarVisiblity` builds the toggle in `convertToMenu`: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/abc6a78ed68f9e8bc9d54e27851093bd687a1cb7/src/resources/formats/html/quarto.js#L345-L456

**Scope:** the same function also makes the left sidebar toggle (`#quarto-sidebarnav-toggle`). On https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/article-layout.html at 1440x900, after a scroll, axe reports `region` on both toggles. I did not do the keyboard tests on the sidebar toggle.

**Fix:** make the toggle a `<button aria-expanded aria-controls>` inside a named `nav`. Hide the original items with `visibility: hidden` or `inert`, not with `opacity`.

## Steps to reproduce

`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website
website:
  title: TOC collapse
format:
  html:
    toc: true
```

`index.qmd`:

````qmd
---
title: Visible page-right figure
---

[{{< placeholder 800 300 >}}]{.column-page-right}

## Section A
{{< lipsum 3 >}}

## Section B
{{< lipsum 3 >}}

## Section C
{{< lipsum 3 >}}

## Section D
{{< lipsum 3 >}}

## Section E
{{< lipsum 3 >}}
````

1. Run `quarto preview`.
2. Make the browser window 1440x900.
3. Press Tab again and again.

## Actual behavior

- The "On this page" toggle shows at the top right.
- Tab does not go to the toggle. Enter does not open it.
- Tab stops on the invisible original TOC links. No focus indicator shows.
- The accessibility tree shows the toggle as text only.
- axe-core 4.10.3 reports `region` on `.quarto-sidebar-toggle-title`.

## Expected behavior

- Tab goes to the toggle. Enter or Space opens it.
- The toggle has a button role and an `aria-expanded` state.
- The hidden TOC links are not in the tab order.
- The toggle is inside a landmark.

title: The axe check misses revealjs contrast at desktop viewports
description:
## I have

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of Quarto CLI
- [x] formatted my issue following the Bug Reports guide

## Bug description

In a revealjs deck, the `axe` option reports no `color-contrast` results at desktop viewports. It does report them at a narrow viewport, such as 320x568. The same gap occurs in `quarto call axe`.

At desktop sizes, reveal.js puts the slide backgrounds in a separate `.reveal .backgrounds` layer. This layer is behind the slide text, but it is not an ancestor of the text. As a result, axe cannot find the background color. It marks each text node as "incomplete" with the `bgOverlap` message: "Element's background color could not be determined because it is overlapped by another element".

The `document` and `console` reporters show only `result.violations` ([document](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b3da6484d8296b0febdad0b322c966cff10f262f/src/resources/formats/html/axe/axe-check.js#L328-L344), [console](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b3da6484d8296b0febdad0b322c966cff10f262f/src/resources/formats/html/axe/axe-check.js#L223-L233)). The `json` reporter prints the full result, so the incomplete nodes are there, but they are not marked as a problem ([json](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b3da6484d8296b0febdad0b322c966cff10f262f/src/resources/formats/html/axe/axe-check.js#L213-L215)). `quarto call axe` requests only violations ([scan.ts](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b3da6484d8296b0febdad0b322c966cff10f262f/src/command/call/axe/scan.ts#L279-L294)). Thus, contrast failures in revealjs are not visible.

At 320x568, reveal.js changes to scroll view. In scroll view, the backgrounds are inside the slide, and axe can find the color.

Before the scan, [`revealUnhideSlides()`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b3da6484d8296b0febdad0b322c966cff10f262f/src/resources/formats/html/axe/axe-check.js#L477-L491) removes `hidden` and `aria-hidden` from the slides. It does not change the backgrounds layer.

## Steps to reproduce

````qmd
---
format:
  revealjs:
    axe:
      output: document
footer: "[quarto.org](https://quarto.org)"
---

## Slide

See [the Quarto website](https://quarto.org).

[This grey text fails contrast.]{style="color: #ccc"}
````

Preview and navigate to Accessibility Report slide.

## Actual behavior

At 1440x900, the report shows no `color-contrast` findings. axe marks five nodes as incomplete: the heading, the body text, the grey text, the body link, and the footer link.

| Viewport | `color-contrast` violations | Incomplete nodes |
|---|---|---|
| 1440x900 | none | 5 |
| 1050x700 | none | 5 |
| 1000x660 | none | 5 |
| 320x568 | grey text (1.6:1), footer link (4.43:1) | 0 |

## Expected behavior

The report shows the two contrast failures at all viewports: the grey text at 1.6:1 and the footer link at 4.43:1.

## Your environment

- OS: macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83)

title: a11y: revealjs scrollable code blocks cannot be scrolled by keyboard
description:
Split from #14378, which covers `format: html` only.

WCAG: 2.1.1 Keyboard (A), 2.1.3 Keyboard, No Exception (AAA)
axe rule: `scrollable-region-focusable` — reports the `.scrollable` slide and the reveal-menu `.active-menu-panel`, but **not** the code blocks. The code-block half of this issue is invisible to axe; see below.
Targets: `.reveal pre code`, `.scrollable` slides, reveal-menu `.active-menu-panel`

Repro:

````qmd
---
title: "Scrollable regions in revealjs"
format: revealjs
---

## Wide code block

```python
wide_code = "an_unbroken_token_that_cannot_wrap_and_overflows_the_slide_width_easily"
```

## Tall code block

```python
line_01 = "padding"
line_02 = "padding"
line_03 = "padding"
line_04 = "padding"
line_05 = "padding"
line_06 = "padding"
line_07 = "padding"
line_08 = "padding"
line_09 = "padding"
line_10 = "padding"
line_11 = "padding"
line_12 = "padding"
line_13 = "padding"
line_14 = "padding"
line_15 = "padding"
line_16 = "padding"
line_17 = "padding"
line_18 = "padding"
line_19 = "padding"
line_20 = "padding"
line_21 = "padding"
line_22 = "padding"
line_23 = "padding"
line_24 = "padding"
line_25 = "padding"
```

## Scrollable slide {.scrollable}

- item one
- item two
- item three
- item four
- item five
- item six
- item seven
- item eight
- item nine
- item ten
- item eleven
- item twelve
- item thirteen
- item fourteen
- item fifteen
- item sixteen
- item seventeen
- item eighteen
- item nineteen
- item twenty
````

## Code blocks

[`theme.scss`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/1f4ff1871010c559d33719d4a9251c6afb6e131b/src/resources/formats/revealjs/reveal/css/theme/template/theme.scss#L191-L197) gives `.reveal pre code` `overflow: auto; max-height: 400px`. The scroll container is therefore the `code` element, not the `div.sourceCode` wrapper as in HTML output. At 390x844 the wide block hides 192px to the right and the tall block hides 215px below; `div.sourceCode` and `pre` both measure 0 overflow.

A keyboard user cannot reach that hidden content. Tabbing into the wide block lands on the line-number link for line 1 and leaves `scrollLeft` at 0, so all 192px stay clipped.

**Why axe stays silent.** revealjs turns on code line numbers by default. Pandoc emits a real fragment link per numbered line (`<a href="#cbN-n">`), which is focusable by design — it is how a reader links to a line. Without line numbers Pandoc instead emits a decorative anchor carrying `aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"`. `scrollable-region-focusable` passes any scrollable region containing focusable content, so a numbered block satisfies the rule.

The rule is satisfied, but the region still cannot be scrolled. Line anchors sit at the start of each line, so focusing one never moves the region horizontally: measured `scrollLeft` stays 0 with 192px still clipped. Vertical overflow fares better, since tabbing down the anchors does scroll the block, at a cost of one tab stop per line (25 for the block above).

The focusable anchors are deliberate and are not the bug here. #14655 (fa5f81cf7) added `aria-label` to them and explicitly rejected `aria-hidden`, "since these anchors are real, focusable fragment links, and aria-hidden on a focusable element is itself an accessibility violation." Any fix should keep them focusable.

## Scrollable slides and the menu panel

A `.scrollable` slide is reported by axe (`#scrollable-slide`), as are `body` and `#slide-N` on several quarto-web decks, and the reveal-menu `.active-menu-panel` at both 390x844 and 1440x900.

## Constraints

- revealjs binds the arrow keys to slide navigation, so making a region focusable is not sufficient on its own — the keys that scroll it must not fight slide navigation.
- #14795 (off-screen slides stay tabbable) interacts directly. Adding `tabindex="0"` to scrollers on `.past` and `.future` slides would add more phantom tab stops, while the `inert` fix proposed there would neutralize them. These two want fixing together, or in that order.

Related: #14710 (same rule, the axe report UI on revealjs and dashboard), #14249 (same vendored slide-menu component, different rule), #13574 (prior a11y work on revealjs code line numbers).

Part of #8706.

title: revealjs removes the `href` from code line-number links
description: ## I have: - [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues - [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest) - [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html) ## Bug description For revealjs, Quarto removes the `href` from each code line-number link ([format-reveal.ts](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b3da6484d8296b0febdad0b322c966cff10f262f/src/format/reveal/format-reveal.ts#L847-L856)). The comment says these links "can't work because ids are used for sections". That is no longer true. Since reveal.js 5, links to element ids work ([f8e3406](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/commit/f8e3406327d71b6f07454f7cd90090967ce1bb72), hakimel/reveal.js#3444). Removing the `href` now causes two bugs: 1. **Single file:** `fixEmptyHrefs` ([html.ts](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b3da6484d8296b0febdad0b322c966cff10f262f/src/core/html.ts#L121-L139)) sets `href=""`. A click on a line number, or Enter on it, goes to the title slide. 2. **Website project:** `fixEmptyHrefs` is skipped ([pandoc.ts](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/b3da6484d8296b0febdad0b322c966cff10f262f/src/command/render/pandoc.ts#L615-L628)), so the anchor has no `href`. A click or Enter stays on the slide, stepped `code-line-numbers` highlights are not changed, and axe reports no line-number problems in either project type. title: a11y: narrow-viewport sidebar toolbar is a nav landmark with no links
description:
The bar that appears below the navbar under the `lg` breakpoint is marked up as a
`nav`, so it becomes a navigation landmark. It holds the sidebar toggle button,
the page title or the breadcrumbs, and the search button. In neither
configuration does the `nav` itself hold a navigation link.

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/093316c3348715aab8447bd09faa2eca0ca0e98a/src/resources/projects/website/templates/nav-before-body.ejs#L63-L89

- With breadcrumbs on (the default), every link is inside a nested
  `nav.quarto-page-breadcrumbs`, which is its own landmark. The postprocessor
  swaps it in for the title element:
  https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/093316c3348715aab8447bd09faa2eca0ca0e98a/src/project/types/website/website-navigation.ts#L470-L482
- With `breadcrumbs: false` there are no links at all. The `<a>` at L74 and L78
  has no `href`. It is a Bootstrap collapse trigger, and #14826 already removed
  the `role="navigation"` and `role="link"` it used to carry.

So the landmark holds a button, a heading, and another landmark.

The strip only exists below `lg`, and the sidebar it toggles is a collapse that
sits under it, so both are in the accessibility tree together when a reader opens
the sidebar:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/093316c3348715aab8447bd09faa2eca0ca0e98a/src/resources/projects/website/navigation/quarto-nav.scss#L454-L493

This surfaced in review of #14813, which gives every `nav` landmark a distinct
`aria-label`. Naming this one is hard because there is no honest navigation word
for it. The label there is `Toolbar`, which a screen reader announces as
"Toolbar, navigation".

axe does not flag this. `landmark-unique` only requires that the labels differ,
which #14813 satisfies. This is a markup question, not a rule violation.

## Suggested fix

Change the `nav` to a `div` and drop its `aria-label`. The nested breadcrumbs
`nav` keeps its own landmark and label, so the only difference for a reader is
that the `Toolbar` entry drops out of the landmark list. Nothing else moves, and
no links become unreachable.

Points to check:

- Most CSS selectors are class based (`.quarto-secondary-nav`), but four rules
  use the element selector `nav.quarto-secondary-nav` and need updating.
- With `breadcrumbs: false` the bar then holds no landmark at all. Make sure the
  page title inside it is still reachable.
- The `navigation-toolbar-label` language key added by #14813 becomes unused. It
  ships in `_language.yml` and in all 33 translated files, so remove it before
  1.11 is released rather than after.

Split from #14813. Part of #8706.

Investigated with AI (Claude Code), grounded in a local clone.

title: Revealjs line highlighting cannot meet WCAG contrast
description:
In revealjs, `code-line-numbers` highlights lines by fading the other lines to `opacity: 0.4` ([line-highlight.css#L1-L7](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/abc6a78ed68f9e8bc9d54e27851093bd687a1cb7/src/resources/formats/revealjs/plugins/line-highlight/line-highlight.css#L1-L7)). The design comes from the reveal.js highlight plugin, which uses the same value.

At 0.4, the faded lines fail [WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#contrast-minimum). With the default highlight theme on a white background, faded tokens are 1.7:1 to 2.6:1. The requirement is 4.5:1.

No other opacity value is a good fix. The token colors of the theme are close to 4.5:1 at full opacity, so they have almost no room to fade:

| Token | Color | Contrast at 1.0 | Contrast at 0.4 | Minimum opacity for 4.5:1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| attribute (`.at`) | #657422 | 5.15 | 1.74 | 0.94 |
| import (`.im`) | #00769e | 5.14 | 1.81 | 0.93 |
| comment (`.co`) | #5e5e5e | 6.48 | 1.85 | 0.85 |
| plain text | #111111 | 18.88 | 2.62 | 0.58 |

At 0.94, the highlighted line looks the same as the other lines. The feature then has no function.

The faded text is not exempt. WCAG gives an exemption only for "incidental" text, and the faded lines are content that the audience reads for context. Sometimes an earlier step shows all the lines at full opacity (`code-line-numbers="|2|4-5"`). This does not help a person in the audience, because that person cannot go back to the earlier step.

### Suggestions

1. **Documentation:** In the [Line Highlighting](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/#line-highlighting) section, tell authors that the fade does not meet WCAG contrast. Tell authors who need accessible slides not to use `code-line-numbers` for this purpose.
2. **Investigate other methods:** Show emphasis on the highlighted lines and keep the other lines at full contrast. Some possible methods are a background color, a left border, or a bold font weight. A method that uses only color must also meet [1.4.11 Non-text Contrast](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#non-text-contrast) and [1.4.1 Use of Color](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#use-of-color). This can be a new default or an option.

### Repro

````qmd
---
format: revealjs
---

## Python

```{.python code-line-numbers="2|4-5"}
import numpy as np  # a comment
x = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
def f(x, k=2):
    """Docstring here."""
    return x ** k + 3.5
```
````

Quarto 1.11.4, default revealjs theme. The contrast values come from the computed styles in Chrome.

AI tools helped with this investigation. The investigation used a local clone of quarto-cli (see "Using AI tools to investigate" in CONTRIBUTING.md).

title: Notebook previews don't pick up options from a custom format extension
description:
### I have

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of Quarto CLI
- [x] formatted my issue following the Bug Reports guide

### Bug description

When a page embeds a notebook cell with `{{< embed >}}`, Quarto also builds a preview page for that notebook.
I noticed that if the project uses a custom format from an extension, the preview doesn't get that format's options.
The host page and the notebook's own page get them just fine.
With the built-in `html` format, the preview gets the same options as the other pages, which is what I'd expect.

I'm not completely sure this isn't intended, but it does feel like a bug.

I think it comes from `renderHtmlNotebook` in `src/render/notebook/notebook-contributor-html.ts`.
It renders the preview with `formats: ["html"]` and only carries over the host format's `theme`, so the rest of a custom format's options are left behind.

I ran into this while moving the quarto.org theme into a local extension.
The notebook previews there lost the header and footer scripts that the site's format adds.

### Steps to reproduce

Here's a small project with four files, and none of them need a computation engine.

`_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: default

format: myformat-html
```

`_extensions/myformat/_extension.yml`:

```yaml
title: My Format
author: Example
version: 1.0.0
contributes:
  formats:
    html:
      include-in-header:
        text: '<meta name="from-myformat" content="yes">'
```

`index.qmd`:

````qmd
---
title: "Host page"
---

{{< embed notebook.ipynb#cell-hello >}}
````

`notebook.ipynb`:

```json
{
 "cells": [
  {
   "cell_type": "raw",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "---\n",
    "title: Notebook\n",
    "---"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "c1",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "hello\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "#| label: cell-hello\n",
    "print(\"hello\")"
   ]
  }
 ],
 "metadata": {
  "kernelspec": {
   "display_name": "Python 3",
   "language": "python",
   "name": "python3"
  }
 },
 "nbformat": 4,
 "nbformat_minor": 5
}
```

Then render it and look for the tag in each page:

```bash
quarto render
grep -c 'from-myformat' index.html notebook.html notebook-preview.html
```

### Actual behavior

The tag from the custom format is missing from the preview:

```text
index.html:1
notebook.html:1
notebook-preview.html:0
```

### Expected behavior

I'd expect the preview to get the custom format's options, like the other two pages:

```text
index.html:1
notebook.html:1
notebook-preview.html:1
```

That's exactly what happens with the built-in format.
If you swap `format: myformat-html` in `_quarto.yml` for the following, all three pages have the tag:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    include-in-header:
      text: '<meta name="from-myformat" content="yes">'
```

title: Text in revealjs presentations cannot be resized
description:
A reader cannot make the text in a revealjs presentation larger. This fails [WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#resize-text). I am filing this to record the problem. I do not have a fix to propose.

## Browser zoom has no effect

Reveal.js scales each slide to fit the viewport. When a reader zooms in with the browser controls, the viewport gets smaller in CSS pixels, and reveal.js scales the slide down to fit it. The text stays the same size on screen. Scroll view has the same result.

To see this, render any deck, open it in a desktop browser, and zoom to 200%:

````qmd
---
title: "Zoom"
format: revealjs
---

## Slide

Some text.
````

## The template also disables pinch-zoom

The revealjs template hard-codes `maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no` in the viewport meta tag:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/6e7f7caedb6eea77662ac6041310a858e254ccea/src/resources/formats/revealjs/pandoc/revealjs.template#L18-L18

```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, maximum-scale=1.0, user-scalable=no, minimal-ui">
```

axe reports this tag on every deck (critical, WCAG 2.0 AA 1.4.4, rule `meta-viewport`):

> Zooming and scaling must not be disabled
>
> user-scalable=no on <meta> tag disables zooming on mobile devices

Removing `user-scalable=no` clears the axe finding. It does not by itself make text larger, because reveal.js still scales the slide to fit. I did not test pinch-zoom on a device.

## Workaround for authors

The [quarto-revealjs-a11y](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-revealjs-a11y) extension adds font-size controls for readers. It also rewrites the viewport tag to `width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0` when the page loads.

---

Quarto 1.11.4, macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83).

> Investigation was AI-assisted, grounded in a local clone of quarto-cli, per CONTRIBUTING.md's note on using AI tools.

title: Typst: image size in px is not converted when the image has fig-alt
description:
### Bug description

When I render to Typst, an image with `fig-alt` keeps its size in `px`. Typst has no `px` unit, so compiling the document fails with `invalid number suffix: px`. The same image without `fig-alt` renders fine, because Quarto converts its size to inches.

The cause is in the Typst filter, `quarto-post/typst.lua`. When an image has alt text, the filter doesn't pass it on to Pandoc. It writes the Typst `image()` call itself as a `RawInline` and copies the `height` and `width` values across unchanged. The filter does convert sizes before that, but only when they're plain numbers. `tonumber("200px")` returns `nil`, so `200px` ends up in the Typst code as it is.

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/03f0fdf586b066ffa81ebefa55e5dad21e08bec0/src/resources/filters/quarto-post/typst.lua#L218-L225

This is where the filter builds the `image()` call for an image with alt text:

- https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/03f0fdf586b066ffa81ebefa55e5dad21e08bec0/src/resources/filters/quarto-post/typst.lua#L262-L273

An image without alt text goes through Pandoc's Typst writer instead, and that writer turns pixel sizes into inches:

- https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/blob/9376458c26d25d222e5a898ede254ebb2f47ffbe/src/Text/Pandoc/Writers/Typst.hs#L555-L563

Sizes in `%` still work with `fig-alt`, because Typst understands `%`.

### Checked against Pandoc

I also ran the same image through Pandoc on its own, and Pandoc isn't the cause. The Pandoc 3.10 bundled with Quarto converts the size and writes the alt text correctly:

```bash
printf 'A ![](https://quarto.org/quarto.png){height="200px" alt="Quarto logo."} b\n' | quarto pandoc -f markdown -t typst
# #box(image("https://quarto.org/quarto.png", height: 2.08333in, alt: "Quarto logo."))
```

A comment in the filter says the raw `image()` call is a workaround, because Pandoc used to leave alt text out of Typst output (jgm/pandoc#11394). Pandoc 3.10 writes `alt:` itself now, so the workaround might not be needed any more. For the moment, it's the code path that causes this bug.

### Steps to reproduce

````qmd
---
format: typst
keep-typ: true
---

![](https://quarto.org/quarto.png){height="200px"}

![](https://quarto.org/quarto.png){height="200px" fig-alt="Quarto logo."}
````

### Actual behavior

The generated `.typ` file has these two lines:

```typst
#box(image("t3_files/mediabag/quarto.png", height: 2.08333in))
#box(image("t3_files/mediabag/quarto.png", alt: "Quarto logo.", height: 200px))
```

Typst then stops with this error:

```text
error: invalid number suffix: `px`
```

### Expected behavior

I'd expect the image with `fig-alt` to have its size converted just like the one without it:

```typst
#box(image("t3_files/mediabag/quarto.png", alt: "Quarto logo.", height: 2.08333in))
```

I can see two ways to fix it. The filter could convert `px` values to inches with `PANDOC_WRITER_OPTIONS.dpi`, as it already does for plain numbers. Or, now that Pandoc 3.10 writes the alt text itself, the filter could let Pandoc handle these images as well.

### Your environment

I'm on macOS. The bug happens with Quarto 1.10.18 and with the current `main` branch at commit 03f0fdf586b066ffa81ebefa55e5dad21e08bec0.

title: revealjs logo option's alt text support is undocumented
description:
# revealjs logo option's alt text support is undocumented

The `logo` option for `format: revealjs` accepts an object form with `path`
and `alt` fields, and the `alt` value renders as the image's `alt`
attribute. The reference and guide pages show only the string form and never
mention `alt` text.

This YAML gives the logo an accessible name:

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    logo:
      path: logo.png
      alt: "Company logo"
```

The docs pages I checked show only the plain string form and say nothing
about `alt`:

- <https://quarto.org/docs/reference/formats/presentations/revealjs.html>
  — the `logo` entry reads "Logo image (placed in bottom right corner of
  slides)", with no example and no mention of an object form.
- <https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/index.html> (section
  "Footer & Logo") — the only example is `logo: logo.png`.

title: Plotly figures in initially hidden tabs of a panel-tabset don't fill the tab width
description:
### I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

### Bug description

**Update:** this is a duplicate of #4705. A fix for the width problem is in #14940.

Plotly figures in any tab other than the one active on page load don't fill the width of the tab. They render at Plotly's default size (700px wide, 450px tall) and only resize when the browser window is resized (e.g. by zooming in or out).

As far as I can tell, the cause is:

- Plotly.js resizes `responsive` figures (plotly.py sets `responsive: true` by default) from a `window` `resize` listener.
- Figures in hidden tabs are drawn while their container has no width, so they fall back to the 700px default.
- When a tab is shown, `src/resources/formats/html/quarto.js` dispatches a `slideenter` event (for htmlwidgets), but no `window` `resize` event, so Plotly never re-measures the figure.

This was previously raised in discussion #2082. I misfiled it in [quarto-dev/quarto#876](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto/issues/876), which I'll close in favour of #4705.

I used an AI assistant (Claude Code, with a local clone of this repository) to help investigate. I've reproduced the problem and checked the measurements below on my own machine.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Save the document below as `plotly-tabset.qmd` and run `quarto preview plotly-tabset.qmd`.
2. In the browser window that opens (wider than about 900px), click "Tab 2".

Opening the rendered HTML file directly from disk also shows the problem. However, Chrome and Safari don't run Quarto's JavaScript for local files (`quarto.js` is loaded as a module), so a fix can't be checked that way unless the document uses `embed-resources: true`.

````qmd
---
title: "Plotly in a tabset"
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full
engine: jupyter
---

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Tab 1

```{python}
import plotly.graph_objects as go

go.Figure(go.Scatter(x=[1, 2, 3], y=[1, 3, 2]))
```

## Tab 2

```{python}
go.Figure(go.Scatter(x=[1, 2, 3], y=[1, 3, 2]))
```

:::
````

### Actual behavior

The figure in Tab 2 is 700px wide and 450px tall (Plotly's defaults), while the tab is wider. It only fills the tab after the browser window is resized, e.g. by zooming in or out.

The figure in Tab 1 fills the tab correctly, at the 525px height plotly.py sets.

### Expected behavior

The figure in Tab 2 fills the width of the tab as soon as the tab is shown, as the figure in Tab 1 does.

### Your environment

- IDE: none (`quarto render` and `quarto preview` in a terminal)
- OS: macOS 27.0 (26A428)
- Browsers: Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (Safari)
- Quarto: 1.11.5 (latest pre-release). Also reproduced on 1.10.18 (latest release).
- Python 3.13.15, plotly 7.1.0 (bundles plotly.js 4.0.0), Jupyter 5.9.1. Also reproduced with plotly 6.6.0.
- Quarto 1.11.5 was run from the extracted release tarball, with Python from a clean virtual environment, which is why `quarto check` shows temporary paths.

title: Update the bundled Observable Plot and Inputs libraries
description:
Quarto bundles Observable Plot 0.6.11 and Observable Inputs 0.10.6. These versions have not changed since November 2023.

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/e24bcbd1fa93165e4dc2b022a9564dbc1692f114/src/resources/formats/html/ojs/quarto-ojs-runtime.js#L207-L208

Before that, the bundled Plot moved about every six months: 0.6.0 (November 2022), 0.6.5 (April 2023), and 0.6.11 (November 2023, [f04ca43](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/commit/f04ca4333d)).

The current Plot release is 0.6.17. The upstream `observablehq/stdlib` pins Plot 0.6.16 and Inputs 0.11.0 ([stdlib v5.8.8](https://github.com/observablehq/stdlib/commit/493bf210f5fcd9360cf87a961403aa963ba08c96)).

### Accessibility

An update also removes some accessibility errors on quarto.org.

In Plot 0.6.11, each axis tick is in the accessibility tree. VoiceOver announces each tick as "image", which adds noise between the tick values ([observablehq/plot#2019](https://github.com/observablehq/plot/issues/2019)). Plot 0.6.14 hides the ticks from assistive technology ([observablehq/plot#2018](https://github.com/observablehq/plot/pull/2018)).

The tick groups also have an `aria-label` with no role. axe reports this as `aria-prohibited-attr`, a failure of [WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#name-role-value).

I scanned the 10 OJS pages on quarto.org with `quarto call axe`, before and after the documented import of the latest Plot (0.6.17):

| | Plot findings | instances |
|---|---|---|
| Plot 0.6.11 (bundled) | 20 | 54 |
| Plot 0.6.17 (import) | 10 | 24 |

The update removed all findings on axis-tick and grid groups. It added no new findings. I did not test Inputs 0.11.0.

### If your own scan found these errors

Charts from Plot 0.6.11 give `aria-prohibited-attr` errors on `<g>` elements such as `g[aria-label="y-axis tick"]`. These errors come from Plot, not from your content.

To use a newer Plot on a page, add this cell ([Libraries](https://quarto.org/docs/interactive/ojs/libraries.html#stdlib)):

``` js
Plot = import("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@observablehq/plot/+esm")
```

The newer Plot still puts an `aria-label` on data marks (`rect`, `frame`, `line`, `rule`, `tick`). axe reports these marks with the same error. A Quarto update does not change this.

This is a design decision in Plot. Plot gives every mark an automatic label, such as "dot", and adds no role ([observablehq/plot#710](https://github.com/observablehq/plot/pull/710)). One Plot maintainer's view is that SVG-AAM already includes a `<g>` with a non-empty `aria-label` in the accessibility tree. The maintainer was not sure that `role="graphics-object"` would help users ([observablehq/plot#944](https://github.com/observablehq/plot/issues/944#issuecomment-1158403221)). The open request for a role is [observablehq/plot#1760](https://github.com/observablehq/plot/issues/1760).

Plot's `ariaHidden` mark option removes a decorative mark from the accessibility tree ([Plot accessibility docs](https://github.com/observablehq/plot/blob/main/docs/features/accessibility.md)). 

AI tools helped with this investigation. The investigation used local clones of `quarto-cli` and `quarto-web`.

title: Code cell numbering in embeds is invisible in dark themes
description:
## I have - [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues - [x] installed the latest version of Quarto CLI - [x] formatted my issue following the Bug Reports guide ## Bug description In dark themes, the cell number (e.g. `In [1]:`, `In [2]:`, ...) from an embedded code cell ends up very dark on a dark background and fails contrast minimums. These cell numbers are a bare `
` inside a `.cell-decorator` div (`
In [2]:
`) — the `
` itself has no class, so its text color comes from an unscoped, generic `pre` rule rather than anything specific to `.cell-decorator`.

Bootstrap's own `pre` rule ([`_reboot.scss#L300`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/e24bcbd1fa93165e4dc2b022a9564dbc1692f114/src/resources/formats/html/bootstrap/dist/scss/_reboot.scss#L300)) sets `color: $pre-color`, which defaults to `$body-emphasis-color` ([`_variables.scss#L1774-L1775`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/e24bcbd1fa93165e4dc2b022a9564dbc1692f114/src/resources/formats/html/bootstrap/dist/scss/_variables.scss#L1774-L1775)) — a light-mode-oriented near-black. Quarto's own override ([`_bootstrap-rules.scss#L949-L953`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/e24bcbd1fa93165e4dc2b022a9564dbc1692f114/src/resources/formats/html/bootstrap/_bootstrap-rules.scss#L949-L953)) resets `background-color` to `initial` (so `.cell-decorator`'s bare `
` blends into the page) but never resets `color`, so the hardcoded near-black text is left sitting on whatever background the page inherits.

Bootstrap's own dark themes carry a defensive fix for exactly this: [`darkly.scss#L184`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/e24bcbd1fa93165e4dc2b022a9564dbc1692f114/src/resources/formats/html/bootstrap/themes/darkly.scss#L184) and [`cyborg.scss#L192`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/e24bcbd1fa93165e4dc2b022a9564dbc1692f114/src/resources/formats/html/bootstrap/themes/cyborg.scss#L192) both set `$pre-color: inherit !default;`. 

## Steps to reproduce

````qmd
---
title: "Repro"
theme: dark.scss
---

{{< embed source.qmd#cell-one >}}
````

with `dark.scss`:

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$body-bg: #151515;
$body-color: #f8f8f8;

/*-- scss:rules --*/
```

and `source.qmd`:

````qmd
---
title: "Source"
---

```{r}
#| label: cell-one
1 + 1
```
````

`quarto render index.qmd`

## Actual behavior

The compiled theme CSS resolves to:

```css
pre{...color:#000;background-color:#f8f9fa;...}
pre{background-color:initial;padding:initial;border:initial}
```

`.cell-decorator`'s `
` ends up with `color: #000` on the page's
`$body-bg` (`#151515`) — a contrast ratio of ~1.15:1.



## Expected behavior

`.cell-decorator`'s `
` text should meet 4.5:1 contrast against the
theme's own background, the same way Bootswatch's dark themes handle it.



**Author workaround (that generated screenshot):** add `$pre-color: inherit !default;` to the theme's
`scss:defaults` block:

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$body-bg: #151515;
$body-color: #f8f8f8;
$pre-color: inherit !default;
/*-- scss:rules --*/
```

title: `--profile` missing from `quarto call engine`, `call build-ts-extension`, and `call typst-gather` --help
description:
`quarto call engine`, `quarto call build-ts-extension`, and `quarto call typst-gather --help` are all missing `--profile`, while `quarto call axe --help` has it:

```
$ quarto call typst-gather --help
...
Options:

  -h, --help               - Show this help.
  --init-config            - Generate a starter typst-gather.toml in current directory
  --log          <file>    - Path to log file
  --log-level    <level>   - Log level (debug, info, warning, error, critical)
  --log-format   <format>  - Log format (plain, json-stream)
  --quiet                  - Suppress console output.

$ quarto call axe --help
...
  --log         <file>       - Path to log file
  --log-level   <level>      - Log level (debug, info, warning, error, critical)
  --log-format  <format>     - Log format (plain, json-stream)
  --quiet                    - Suppress console output.
  --profile                  - Active project profile(s)
```

`--profile` is registered as a global option in `appendProfileArg`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/97f222ff3934fa6291272cbf2d969405c636035b/src/quarto-core/profile.ts#L35-L42

This relies on cliffy's native `global: true` option inheritance, which per #8438 does not reliably reach every subcommand. `appendLogOptions` hit the same bug and works around it by manually forwarding the log/quiet options to every subcommand instead of trusting cliffy's inheritance:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/97f222ff3934fa6291272cbf2d969405c636035b/src/core/log.ts#L81-L99

`appendProfileArg` never got the same treatment, so it still depends on cliffy's inheritance and only reaches the last subcommand registered under `call`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/97f222ff3934fa6291272cbf2d969405c636035b/src/command/call/cmd.ts#L7-L20

`axe` was added last (#14815) and is the only one that got `--profile` by coincidence. This also explains why quarto-web's automated reference docs lost `--profile` from `quarto call typst-gather` between v1.11.3 and v1.11.5, even though nothing in `typst-gather`'s own command changed.

We could apply the same subcommand-forwarding pattern from `appendLogOptions` to `appendProfileArg`.

Related: #8438

title: [knitr] custom engine setting asis output does not remove all divs
description:
Here is a demo of using a custom engine in **knitr** which is meant to output raw content. (More details at https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/9163). 
So the engine sets `output: asis` internally (`results: asis` in knitr context)

````markdown
---
title: "Test"
format: 
  typst:
    keep-typ: true
    keep-md: true
---

```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::knit_engines$set(demo = function(options) {

    options[["results"]] <- "asis"

    knitr::engine_output(
      options,
      options$code,
      out = "Should be `asis` content."
    )
  })
```

## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document.

```{demo}
Do no matter
```
````

This is the intermediate .md

````markdown
::: {.cell}

```{.demo .cell-code}
Do no matter
```


Should be `asis` content.
:::

`````

The output wrapping is correctly removed (i.e ``  ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}`` and fenced code block. 

However `` ::: {.cell} `` is still there. 

In code base, we decide to add the wrapping div on condition 
https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/f43107222f70ca3579a520d496597b75b5bd0097/src/resources/rmd/hooks.R#L400-L415

But this is done in the `chunk` hook - and in fact **knitr** does not get the modified options from cell at this point. It could be an issue from **knitr** itself. 

For now, it means that `output: asis` needs to explicitly be set on a cell that should not have the output div.

title: `use binder` asset `vscode.svg` has mismatched mask units, causing macOS thumbnailing to allocate terabytes of RAM
description:
### I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of Quarto CLI (reproduced on 1.10.18, and confirmed the file is unchanged on `main`)
- [x] formatted my issue following the Bug Reports guide

### Bug description

`src/resources/use/binder/vscode.svg` contains a `<mask>` whose units and values disagree:

```xml
<mask id="mask-2" maskContentUnits="userSpaceOnUse" maskUnits="objectBoundingBox"
      x="-15" y="-15" width="1009.27778" height="1006.4">
```

`maskUnits="objectBoundingBox"` means `x`/`y`/`width`/`height` are **fractions of the object bounding box**, but the values are plainly user-space pixel values (they match the `<rect>` on the next line, which is correctly declared `userSpaceOnUse`). This looks like a Sketch export artifact.

Taken literally, against the ~980x980 bounding box, the mask region is:

```
~989,000 x ~986,000 px  =  ~9.8e11 pixels  =  ~3.5 TiB at 4 bytes/px
```

Browsers clamp this, so web output is unaffected and the bug is invisible in normal Quarto use. macOS ImageIO does not clamp. It allocates the region in 128 MiB tiles, so any macOS process that thumbnails or rasterizes this file (Finder, Spotlight, QuickLook, `sips`) balloons until the kernel kills it.

Because QuickLook treats the kill as a transient failure, it respawns and retries indefinitely. On my machine this pinned load average above 400 and drove the system into swap thrash until I tracked it down. `vmmap` on one extension instance:

```
Physical footprint: 162.1G
REGION TYPE           VIRTUAL  RESIDENT   DIRTY   SWAPPED  COUNT
CG Image               162.1G     14.6G   14.6G    147.5G   1297
```

1,297 regions of exactly 128 MiB, which is the tiled allocation of that mask surface.

### Steps to reproduce

No Quarto invocation is needed. The shipped asset alone reproduces it on macOS:

```bash
# fetch the file exactly as shipped
curl -sO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/main/src/resources/use/binder/vscode.svg

# rasterize it with any macOS ImageIO consumer.
# NOTE: this is capped at 3 GB on purpose. Without the watchdog it will
# consume all available RAM and drive the machine into swap thrash.
sips -s format png --out out.png vscode.svg & P=$!
while R=$(ps -o rss= -p $P 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '); [ -n "$R" ]; do
  echo "RSS: $((R/1024)) MB"
  [ "$R" -gt 3145728 ] && { kill -9 $P; echo "runaway, killed"; break; }
  sleep 1
done
```

A 2,380 byte file reaches **12.6 GB RSS within 2 seconds** if left uncapped.

In normal use the trigger is simply having Quarto installed and letting Finder or Spotlight touch `share/use/binder/`, which is what happened here.

### Actual behavior

Rasterizing the shipped `vscode.svg` allocates unbounded memory (observed 162 GB physical footprint) until the process is killed. Under QuickLook this becomes an infinite respawn loop that degrades the whole machine.

### Expected behavior

The asset rasterizes in a few MB, like every other SVG Quarto ships.

### Suggested fix

Delete the incorrect `maskUnits` and its associated values, and let the SVG defaults apply (`objectBoundingBox` with `-10%`/`-10%`/`120%`/`120%`), which comfortably covers the artwork plus its 30 unit stroke:

```diff
-        <mask id="mask-2" maskContentUnits="userSpaceOnUse" maskUnits="objectBoundingBox" x="-15" y="-15" width="1009.27778" height="1006.4">
+        <mask id="mask-2" maskContentUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
```

Verification I ran on this change:

- **Visually lossless.** Headless Chrome renders of the original and the patched file are byte-for-byte identical: 0 differing pixels out of 1,028,180.
- **Memory safe.** Peak RSS drops from >12 GB to 1-2 MB, tested at 32, 128, 512 and 2048 px output.
- I also tested explicit `maskUnits="userSpaceOnUse"` with a widened region; it is equally correct, but the above needs no magic numbers. Note that keeping `userSpaceOnUse` with the *existing* width/height is subtly wrong: it clips the outer white stroke by a few pixels at the edges.

The file has been unchanged since it was added in 411ebc3d ("Baseline implementation of re-entrant quarto use binder command", 2023-09-06), so this affects all releases since.

Happy to open a PR if useful.

### Your environment

- IDE: n/a (reproduced from the shell)
- OS: macOS 27.0 (build 26A428), Apple Silicon (arm64)

title: css-code-annotation smoke test breaks against knitr dev/master, not yet in a knitr release
description:
The smoke test `tests/docs/smoke-all/2023/01/31/css-code-annotation.qmd` started failing on CI (`.code-annotation-container-grid` missing) on both `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest`, starting with the push run at commit 572b946c6 on 2026-09-18. The last known-good push run was at a79a39a9 on 2026-09-11.

For an annotated `{css}` chunk (annotation = trailing `/* <1> */` comment), the entire annotation markup is missing from the rendered HTML, not just a class. No `<dl>`, no `code-annotation-anchor`, no `code-annotation-target` span, plain Pandoc ids (`cb1`, `cb2`) instead of our annotation-aware ids (`annotated-cell-N`).

This isn't caused by a quarto-cli change. `tests/renv.lock` is byte-identical between the last-green and first-red runs. Our CI (`test-smokes.yml`) and `tests/configure-test-env.ps1`/`.sh` deliberately overwrite `knitr`/`rmarkdown` from `yihui.r-universe.dev`'s dev channel after `renv::restore()`, so CI's knitr version is unpinned and rolling rather than the one pinned in `renv.lock`. yihui/knitr@dd0f913f2 (merged 2026-09-17, not in a knitr release yet, current release is 1.52 from 2026-09-06) landed on that dev channel and got pulled in by the next CI run.

I confirmed this by a direct local A/B render, same quarto-cli checkout, only the installed knitr ref changed:

- yihui/knitr@793a020c1 (parent of dd0f913f2): annotation markup present, `.code-annotation-container-grid` present.
- yihui/knitr@dd0f913f2: annotation markup entirely absent.

I've opened yihui/knitr#2488 upstream with a minimal pure-knitr reproducer and the mechanism: `eng_html_asset` (backs the `css`/`js` engines) and `eng_sxss` (`sass`/`scss`) force `options$results <- 'asis'` internally before calling `engine_output()`, and since dd0f913f2 that now reaches the `chunk` hook unconditionally, overriding whatever an `opts_hooks` callback set earlier. That's exactly what our own `chunk` hook relies on:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/c912ed669e5486cc0999060cb5a875dfae5c926f/src/resources/rmd/hooks.R#L811-L822

`knitr_options_hook` forces `results = 'hold'` whenever it detects an inline annotation marker, specifically so our `chunk` hook (not the engine) decides how to wrap the output. For `css`/`scss`/`sass` chunks that override no longer takes effect once knitr picks up dd0f913f2.

Since the current knitr release doesn't have this yet, nobody on a released knitr/quarto-cli combination is affected today. This only shows up because our own CI intentionally runs against knitr's dev channel. We'll want to:

1. See how yihui/knitr#2488 gets resolved upstream, and confirm the fix (whenever it ships) actually restores our annotation grids before it reaches a knitr release.
2. Separately decide whether `hooks.R`'s override should be made more defensive against an engine overriding `results` after the `opts_hooks` callback runs, independent of the upstream fix.

I'll leave a note that #14909 was opened automatically against the CI failure and diagnoses an unrelated pre-existing issue in `format-html.ts`, it doesn't fix this.

title: DecoratedCodeBlock has no docx/pptx renderer — code chunk `filename` header silently dropped
description:
## Summary

A code block decorated with a `filename` (e.g. `{r filename="hello.R"}` or a `.filename` attribute) renders correctly in HTML, LaTeX, and Markdown output, but the filename header is silently dropped for **docx** and **pptx** (and any other format with no dedicated renderer registered).

## Where the gap is

`src/resources/filters/customnodes/decoratedcodeblock.lua` registers exactly four renderers for the `DecoratedCodeBlock` custom AST node:

1. A **default/fallback** renderer (predicate always `true`) — walks the code block for folding only:
   ```lua
   _quarto.ast.add_renderer("DecoratedCodeBlock",
     function(_) return true end,
     function(node)
       return _quarto.ast.walk(node.code_block, { CodeBlock = render_folded_block })
     end)
   ```
2. A markdown renderer (`_quarto.format.isMarkdownOutput()`)
3. A latex renderer (`_quarto.format.isLatexOutput()`)
4. An html renderer (`_quarto.format.isHtmlOutput()`)

Only the html and latex renderers actually read `node.filename` and render a header for it. Since docx/pptx match none of the three specific predicates, they fall through to the **default renderer**, which never reads `node.filename` (or `node.caption`) at all — it only walks for `render_folded_block` (itself a no-op for non-HTML output). The result: the code block content survives, but the filename header silently disappears, with no warning.

## Repro

```markdown
---
title: repro
---

```{.python filename="hello.py"}
print("hello")
```
```

Render with `quarto render repro.qmd --to docx` (or `--to pptx`). The code block appears; the "hello.py" filename header does not. Compare with `--to html` or `--to latex`, both of which show it.

## Suggested fix

Add a docx/pptx-aware renderer for `DecoratedCodeBlock` (or extend the default renderer to check `_quarto.format.isDocxOutput()`/`isPowerPointOutput()`) that emits *some* visible representation of `node.filename` — e.g. a bold paragraph immediately before the code block, mirroring the semantic intent of the html wrapper (`code-with-filename`) and the latex `\caption`, adapted to what Pandoc's docx/pptx writers can represent natively (Word/PowerPoint have no custom CSS to hook into, so this would need to be a plain paragraph/text run rather than a styled wrapper).

## Context

Found while auditing `decoratedcodeblock.lua`'s renderer coverage against Pandoc's non-core output targets (docx/pptx) for a project that reuses these filters. Confirmed against a fresh clone at `v1.11.3` (and current `main`, `83d48d8e8` — the file is unchanged between the two).

website:

title: Typst brand fonts never download a bold-italic face from Google Fonts
description: ## I have: - [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues - [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest) - [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html) ## Bug description For `format: typst`, Quarto downloads the Google fonts named in the brand into `.quarto/typst/fonts/`. When a font entry gives both a `style` and a `weight`, the two never combine. Quarto downloads the weights at normal style and weight 400 at each style. It never downloads a bold-italic face. The result is silent. Typst has no face to use, so `#strong[... #emph[x] ...]` shows italic at regular weight. A brand that asks for a bold-italic heading gets the same. Nothing in the render log says a face is missing. The cause is the URL that Quarto builds for the Google Fonts API. In [`src/command/render/pandoc.ts#L1548-L1560`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/8c87d79047c8378a1e643434891ff100daaa03bb/src/command/render/pandoc.ts#L1548-L1560), the family, the style list, and the weight list are joined with `:` ```ts const parts = [family!]; if (style) { style = Array.isArray(style) ? style : [style]; parts.push(style.join(",")); } if (weight) { weight = Array.isArray(weight) ? weight : [weight]; parts.push(weight.join(",")); } const response = await fetch( `${base_urls[source]}?family=${parts.join(":")}`, ); ``` For `style: [normal, italic]` and `weight: [400, 700]` this gives: ``` https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Atkinson Hyperlegible:normal,italic:400,700 ``` That is not valid syntax for the v1 CSS API. The v1 API expects one comma-separated variant list, in which a weight and a style are one token (`700italic`). The API splits the string on commas and reads each part as a separate variant. The parts here are `normal`, `italic:400` and `700`, so it returns normal 400, italic 400 and normal 700. Two faults follow from this: 1. A weight and a style never combine, so bold italic is unreachable. 2. The first weight in the list is joined to the last style and is lost. For `style: italic` and `weight: [700, 900]` the token `italic:700` returns italic 400, and only 900 arrives as a weight. HTML is not affected. HTML uses a separate code path in [`src/core/sass/brand.ts#L119-L153`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/8c87d79047c8378a1e643434891ff100daaa03bb/src/core/sass/brand.ts#L119-L153), which builds a v2 (`css2`) URL with correct `ital,wght@` pairs. For the same brand it emits `css2?family=Atkinson+Hyperlegible:ital,wght@0,700;1,700`, and that URL does serve italic 700. ## Steps to reproduce Render this document. The brand is in the document YAML, so no `_brand.yml` file is necessary. It asks for two weights at two styles. ````qmd --- title: "Bold italic" format: typst brand: typography: fonts: - family: Atkinson Hyperlegible source: google weight: [400, 700] style: [normal, italic] base: Atkinson Hyperlegible --- Normal. *Italic.* **Bold.** ***Bold italic.*** ```` Then ask Typst which variants it found in the font cache: ```bash quarto typst fonts --variants --font-path .quarto/typst/fonts ``` ## Actual behavior No bold-italic face is in the cache: ``` Atkinson Hyperlegible ├ .../9Bt43C1KxNDXMspQ1lPyU89-1h6ONRlW45G056IqUwU.ttf │ Style: Italic, Weight: 400, Stretch: 100% ├ .../9Bt73C1KxNDXMspQ1lPyU89-1h6ONRlW45G8Wbc9dCWK.ttf │ Style: Normal, Weight: 700, Stretch: 100% └ .../9Bt23C1KxNDXMspQ1lPyU89-1h6ONRlW45G04pIt.ttf Style: Normal, Weight: 400, Stretch: 100% ``` Three faces arrive out of the four requested combinations, and italic 700 is the one that never arrives. All four exist for this family. The render gives no warning, so `***Bold italic.***` shows italic at regular weight. The result is the same when the brand asks for the bold-italic face alone. With `weight: 700` and `style: italic`, one face arrives, and it is `Style: Italic, Weight: 400`. Two separate `fonts:` entries for the same family give the same result. A `_brand.yml` file gives the same result as the document YAML above: both produce an identical `.typ` file. Google does serve the face. This command returns italic 700: ```bash curl -s "https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Atkinson+Hyperlegible:ital,wght@0,400;0,700;1,400;1,700" ``` ## Expected behavior Quarto downloads a face for each combination of the requested weights and styles that exist for the family. For the document above, `quarto typst fonts --variants` also reports `Style: Italic, Weight: 700`. If a combination does not exist for the family, Quarto says so in the render log, as it already does for an unusable font format. ## Your environment - IDE: Positron 1.130.0 - OS: macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83) The fault is also present in the development version. The font fetch is TypeScript that a development build runs from source, and the lines above are unchanged between the `v1.11.4` tag and `main` at 8c87d79. title: Skip link href is rewritten to a cross-document URL on index.html
description:
## I have:

- [x] searched the issue tracker for similar issues
- [x] installed the latest version of [Quarto CLI](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest)
- [x] formatted my issue following the [Bug Reports guide](https://quarto.org/bug-reports.html)

## Bug description

On a website's `index.html`, `quarto-nav.js` rewrites the skip-to-content link so its `href` points at a different document than the page it is on. The link is emitted as a same-document fragment:

```html
<a id="quarto-skip-link" class="visually-hidden-focusable" href="#quarto-document-content">
```

At load time, `quarto-nav.js` walks every `<a>` and strips a trailing `/index.html` from its resolved `href`:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/7ee762a4ceb4c1750660a124e042fecdc073e29d/src/resources/projects/website/navigation/quarto-nav.js#L271-L282

For the skip link, `links[i].href` reads back as the fully resolved URL, so on `http://host/index.html` it is `http://host/index.html#quarto-document-content`. The regex matches `/index.html` followed by `#`, and the href becomes `http://host/#quarto-document-content` — a URL whose path no longer matches the document's.

Two consequences:

1. The link is no longer a same-document fragment, so activating it navigates to `/` and reloads instead of moving focus within the current page. That defeats the purpose of a skip link for keyboard users, which is what #14684 added it for.
2. `axe-core`'s `region` rule exempts skip links from "all page content should be contained by landmarks" only when the href is a same-document fragment. With the rewritten href the exemption is lost, so every scan of a Quarto site reports a `region` violation on `#quarto-skip-link`, on the home page only.

The rewrite is intentional for ordinary navigation links (#14667 refined the regex). It should not apply to links that were authored as bare fragments.

## Steps to reproduce

````qmd
---
title: "Trail Notes"
---

Notes from walking the coast path.
````

With a minimal `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: "Trail Notes"
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Home
```

Then:

```sh
quarto render
quarto call axe _site
```

Or, without the scanner: serve `_site` over HTTP, open `/index.html`, and read `document.getElementById("quarto-skip-link").href` in the console.

## Actual behavior

On `/index.html`, the skip link's href resolves to a different document:

```
href                = http://127.0.0.1:5503/#quarto-document-content
data-original-href  = http://127.0.0.1:5503/index.html#quarto-document-content
```

`quarto call axe _site` reports the `region` violation on the home page and not on any other page:

```
  index.html 1440x900 light                                  3  color-contrast,image-alt,region
  index.html 1440x900 dark                                   2  image-alt,region
  gear.html  1440x900 light                                  0  (none)

  ID                     IMPACT    STANDARD       N  PAGES  STATUS
  region-5ae782          moderate  Best Practice  1  1      new
```

```
**Standard:** Best Practice · **Impact:** moderate · **Signature:** `region :: #quarto-skip-link`

**Problem:** Some page content is not contained by landmarks
```

Pages other than `index.html` are unaffected: their rewrite is a no-op, the href stays same-document, and `region` does not fire. The two pages have identical landmark structure.

## Expected behavior

The skip link keeps a same-document href on every page, including `index.html`. Activating it moves focus to the main content without a navigation, and `axe-core`'s `region` rule continues to exempt it.

Skipping the rewrite for links authored as bare fragments would fix it. The pre-resolution attribute value is available as `links[i].getAttribute("href")`, so a link whose attribute starts with `#` can be left alone.

## Your environment

- IDE: Positron 1.130.0
- OS: macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83)

title: Quarto doesn't recognize same-origin links on Posit Workbench
description:
Clicking a link inside a Quarto preview in Positron on Workbench opens the page in a new browser tab instead of navigating inside the pane.

## Reproducing

Render this dashboard and preview it in Positron's Viewer pane on Workbench:

````
---
title: "Test Dashboard"
format: dashboard
---

# Tab 1

This is a tab

# Tab 2

This is another tab
````

Click Tab 2. The tab switches inside the Viewer, and the whole dashboard also opens in a new browser tab.

The dashboard is the smallest reproduction, but this is not specific to dashboards or to tabs. Any internal link in a Quarto preview is affected, on any deployment that serves the preview through a proxy.

## What's happening

`handleExternalLinks` ([links.ts:14-16](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/src/webui/quarto-preview/src/frame/links.ts#L14-L16)) hooks every link it decides is external, so those clicks can be handed to the browser. It decides by comparing the link's `href` against an `origin` that the preview server infers from the request (`devserverOrigin`, [http-devserver.ts:329](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/src/core/http-devserver.ts#L329)).

On Workbench the server sees `http://localhost:5158` while the browser sees `https://<workbench-host>/s/<session>/p/<token>/…#tab-2`. The comparison is a `startsWith` between those two, so it fails, and every internal link gets hooked and posted as `openExternal`. The two values agree only when the browser reaches the preview at the same address the server sees, which a proxy rules out.

Comparing `window.location.origin` instead of the server-inferred value would classify these correctly, since the code runs in the browser and the browser already knows its own origin.

Tracked on the Positron side as posit-dev/positron#14459.
