title: Option to render display math blocks as images?
description: I use Quarto (and previously just pandoc) at work to write docs that often include LaTeX math blocks. Unfortunately for me, to get anyone to read them, I have to convert them to Google Docs. That often works fine by rendering as .docx, uploading the doc, and converting it to a Google Doc. However, I usually have issues with display math blocks not rendering correctly when converting from docx to Google Docs. I'm thinking about a potential workaround where I could tell Quarto to render those display math blocks as images, so they'd display correctly in Google Docs. Is that already possible? I'd also think a feature like this might be useful in other scenarios outside of just my use case. My current workflow is to render the doc in a different format, screenshot the correctly-rendered math blocks, and paste them into the Google Doc manually. But it would be really nice to be able to automate that step. :) # Example of the rendering issue ``` --- title: "Quarto to Google Docs math example" self-contained: true format: html: toc: true pdf: toc: true docx: toc: false --- Inline math often renders OK: $1 = \sum_{i=1}^n \pi_i$. Math blocks are also sometimes OK: $$ 1 = \sum_{i=1}^n \pi_i. $$ But more complicated ones usually have issues like: $$ \begin{array}{ll} \mbox{minimize} & f(x) \\ \mbox{subject to} & x \in C \end{array} $$ or like this: $$ \begin{aligned} x \in A \\ y \in B \end{aligned} $$ ``` ## Google Docs ![Screen Shot 2022-05-06 at 11 24 47 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/984039/167197776-0b712586-9eea-4682-bffe-45b8b8e9f227.png) ## MS Word on Mac ## PDF ![Screen Shot 2022-05-06 at 11 24 06 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/984039/167197866-55a76aec-efbf-4b0e-bec0-03795eec3d70.png) ## HTML ![Screen Shot 2022-05-06 at 11 23 58 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/984039/167197890-e8a59575-a390-460b-b415-82645b679fe3.png)

title: project-type and project sidebar configurations cannot always merge
description:
### Bug description

The `website.sidebar` configuration is sometimes an array and sometimes an object. When an extension defines a custom website project type and sets some `website.sidebar` properties, that prevents a downstream project from using a different style of sidebar configuration.

For example, the extension may declare some sidebar defaults:

```yaml
contributes:
  project:
    project:
      type: website
    website:
      sidebar:
        style: "floating"
        collapse-level: 1
        pinned: false
````

The project using this extension might try to use [hybrid navigation](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-navigation.html#hybrid-navigation), like the following:

```yaml
  sidebar:
    - title: "Tutorials"
      style: "docked"
      background: light
      contents:
        - tutorials.qmd
        - tutorial-1.qmd
        - tutorial-2.qmd

    - title: "How-To"
      contents:
        - howto.qmd
        # navigation items
```

These two types of sidebar configurations cannot be merged.

An example of an extension which attempted to define the sidebar:

```bash
quarto add posit-dev/product-doc-theme@v1.1.0
```

We have abandoned sidebar configuration in the extension because of this issue.

### Steps to reproduce

_No response_

### Expected behavior

I do not know enough about all the sidebar configuration options to know if two configurations can always be merged. If they can, then that is what should happen. If they cannot be merged, Quarto should produce a message (warning or error) indicating that the extension and project sidebar configurations are incompatible.

### Actual behavior

The extension-provided sidebar configuration appeared to win. The project sidebar configuration is not shown.

title: Automatic footnote identifier prefixing normalizes filenames imperfectly
description:
### Bug description

RStudio’s Markdown [canonicalization](https://quarto.org/docs/visual-editor/markdown.html#canonical-mode), which is provided [by Quarto](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto/blob/f9edec34e53817e9c9f73cb349f524a82bcc6474/packages/editor/src/editor/editor.ts#L771-L791), adds a normalized version of the edited file's name as footnote (and other) identifiers via Pandoc's [`--id-prefix`](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#option--id-prefix) CLI argument. This is a good thing, in principle.

But the filename normalization is very imperfect, I recently discovered. It should be extended to also normalize (i.e. remove) the special characters it currently doesn't touch. See below for an example (note that it is by no means exhaustive, I just typed special characters until I lost interest).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a text file named ``such.a <[{(weird)}]>|@#§°\&%$£:;*+"´`'~=filename - – — RIGHT?!.md`` (this is a totally valid filename on Linux).

1. Paste some Markdown content including at least one footnote in it.

1. Open the file in RStudio and click on <kbd>Visual</kbd> editor mode, then switch back to <kbd>Source</kbd> editor mode and look at the first footnote identifier.

### Expected behavior

Quarto should normalize the above filename to the (footnote) ID prefix:

```
[^such.a-weirdfilename-----right-1]
```

### Actual behavior

Quarto actually normalizes the above filename to the (footnote) ID prefix:

```

title: Vector graphics (htmlwidget) in typst, similar to default pdf
description:
### Bug description

I wish it was possible to render vector-based plots with typst, similar to the crisp quality produced with default pdf. The webshot-solution for typst is far from ready-to-go and requires several tweaks with fig-dpi, and occasionally also fig-width. I have tried with `fig-format: svg` and `prefer-html: true` in vain. 
This is a particularly annoyance with htmlwidget-based graphics such as ggiraph, where the resulting default webshot2 is of low resolution. Sure, one can adjust with `fig-dpi: 450`, but that also explodes the physical size of the figure on the page (should probably be a separate issue, but connects with the above).

  ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, mapping = ggplot2::aes(x=mpg, y=disp)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point()

title: BUG: Additional figure window shown when rendering matplotlib jshtml animation from python code cell
description:
When rendering a JSHTML animation using the matplotlib package an extra blank figure window is shown. 

This also happens in Jupyter in notebook mode and the solution is to close the extra figure window. 

When this is attempted in quarto, no animation is shown (just the animation controls) which is different to the Jupyter behaviour. 

I think it might be to do with the matplotlib backend being used or the logic to do with capturing the figure output but I'm afraid I have tried a number of things and nothing works - as I say, the plt.close() fix is sufficient for rendering in the Jupyter notebook so this change in behaviour is confusing. 

- Is there a sensible way to do this? 
- I don't think this is expected behaviour and it would be great to be able to show animations!

Many thanks.

### Example script:

````
---
title: "Animation Example"
author: "John Doe"
format: revealjs
---

## Simple JS HTML Animation

- This one creates an extra figure..

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams["animation.html"] = "jshtml"
import matplotlib.animation
import numpy as np

t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi)
x = np.sin(t)

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.axis([0, 2 * np.pi, -1, 1])
l, = ax.plot([], [])

def animate(i):
    l.set_data(t[:i], x[:i])

matplotlib.animation.FuncAnimation(fig, animate, frames=len(t))
```

## With plt.close()

- This one stops the extra figure in jupyter but removes the whole animation in quarto..

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams["animation.html"] = "jshtml"
import matplotlib.animation
import numpy as np

t = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi)
x = np.sin(t)

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.axis([0, 2 * np.pi, -1, 1])
l, = ax.plot([], [])

def animate(i):
    l.set_data(t[:i], x[:i])

result = matplotlib.animation.FuncAnimation(fig, animate, frames=len(t))
plt.close()

# Show result
result
```
````

title: Boolean metadata with value `false`  is not passed onto templates
description:
### Bug description

I'm working on a Typst template and have come across an unexpected behaviour.
Unfortunately I don't understand the inner workings of Pandoc and Quarto well enough to determine whether this is expected behaviour and which lines of code it comes from exactly.

### Steps to reproduce

All relevant files can be seen in the develop branch of the following repo: https://github.com/gl-eb/minimal-doc

To reproduce locally:
1. Clone my git repo and switch to the develop branch
```bash
git clone https://github.com/gl-eb/minimal-doc
cd minimal-doc
git switch develop
```
2. Render the example file
```bash
quarto render template.qmd
```

### Expected behavior

The `titleinheader: false` flag is set in the YAML block of [`template.qmd`](https://github.com/gl-eb/minimal-doc/blob/develop/template.qmd). This should result in the document title not being written to the header in the [PDF](https://github.com/gl-eb/minimal-doc/blob/develop/template.pdf).

### Actual behavior

For some reason, the `titleinheader` variable does not make it into the [`template.typ`](https://github.com/gl-eb/minimal-doc/blob/develop/template.typ) file, where it should be written as part of the `#let minimal()` function (line 287). Using quotes (`titleinheader: "false"`) will lead to the expected behaviour. Since the variable is not being set to `false`, the function reverts to the default value of `true`.

The same behaviour is observed with the `toc` variable, that is part of the default Typst template in Quarto. When set to `false` it's not written to the `.typ` file. Since `false` is the default value, it does not matter (and might be by design?).

title: logo-href does not work in sidebar of quarto book
description:
### Bug description

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/6779 mentions that the `logo-href` option has been added to the `sidebar` option of quarto books (previously only `navbar` was supported). However, this does not appear to be working in my minimal example, nor is it listed in the [documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/reference/projects/books.html) (the navbar option is).

### Steps to reproduce

Create a new quarto book using `quarto create`, then edit the `_quarto.yml` file:

```
project:
  type: book

book:
  title: "Quarto Book"
  author: "Norah Jones"
  date: "4/9/2024"
  chapters:
    - index.qmd
    - intro.qmd
    - summary.qmd
    - references.qmd
  sidebar:
    logo: https://quarto.org/quarto.png
    logo-href: https://www.google.com
  

bibliography: references.bib

format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo
  pdf:
    documentclass: scrreprt
```

### Expected behavior

The logo should become a clickable link pointing to the `logo-href` URL in `_quarto.yml`.

### Actual behavior

the logo links back to the index page of the book.

title: Code-Generated R Figures Not Center-Aligned with `format: typst`
description:
### Bug description

When `format: typst`, the execution option `fig-align: center` fails to center-align figures. Instead, figures appear left-aligned. The expected behavior is that figures should be center-aligned when this option is used.

To verify against any potential Quarto-syntax errors, I conducted tests by changing `format: typst` to `format: pdf` in the example QMD files. In this scenario, all figures appeared center-aligned as expected.

Currently, the only method I can think of to achieve the desired effect is to save the figure as a file and then display it using plain Markdown syntax (see example below). However, this workaround is suboptimal as it introduces an additional step and results in a superfluous file.

### Steps to reproduce

Option 1: Using local execution option

````{qmd}
---
title: "How Can Figures Be Center-Aligned?"
format: typst
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(ggplot2)
gg <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()
ggsave("mtcars.svg", plot = gg, width = 4, height = 3)
```


# First Attempt

```{r}
#| label: fig-place-fig-align-in-chunk
#| echo: fenced

gg

### Bug description

The knitr chunk options are not being validated for notebooks. Output is still being printed even if "include: false" is provided.
![Screen Shot 2024-02-08 at 11 46 31](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/assets/21082597/f5b235a0-4d35-4f64-a595-da9d6afad50d)

### Steps to reproduce

test.qmd as part of my manuscript: 
````qmd
---
title: Test as part of manuscript
description: test knitr chunk options
data: last-modified
---
## This should not have anything below
```{r}
#| label: test-include-false
#| include: false
warning("this is a warning")
cat("this is output")
```
## This should have only the output
```{r}
#| label: test-warning-false
#| warning: false
warning("this is a warning")
cat("this is output")
```
````
This is the YAML file for that manuscript:

````yml
project: 
  type: manuscript
execute:
  freeze: auto

format:
  html:
    code-fold: true
    code-tools: true
    toc: true
    comments:
      hypothesis: true
  docx: default
  jats: default
  agu-pdf: default
manuscript: 
  article: index.qmd
  notebooks: 
    - taxonomy.qmd
    - functions.qmd
    - test.qmd
  ````
Here the chunk options behave as expected as a stand-alone document:
````qmd
---
title: Test as stand-alone document
description: test knitr chunk options stand-alone document
data: last-modified
---
## This should not have anything below
```{r}
#| label: test-include-false
#| include: false
warning("this is a warning")
cat("this is output")
```
## This should have only the output
```{r}
#| label: test-warning-false
#| warning: false
warning("this is a warning")
cat("this is output")
```
````


### Expected behavior

With the "include: false" chunk option, the code should be executed, but not shown. Neither should warnings be printed. 

### Actual behavior

Output and warnings are printed in a notebook document.

title: Mermaid subgraphs in a flowchart have a too dark background
description:
### Bug description

I am starting to use mermaid to make flowcharts in my presentations and I just noticed that subgraphs in a mermaid flowchart look quite bad by default, with the subgraph background being really dark and taking over the node backgrounds (the nodes seem to be alpha blended with the dark and so they appear nearly as dark) so the nodes are hard to see. This is fixable with either using a mermaid theme or custom CSS, but it seems like the default should be legible.

### Steps to reproduce

This document demonstrates the issue:

````quarto
---
format: 
  html: default
---

## Subgraph has too dark background

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    c1-->a2
    subgraph ide1 [one]
    a1-->a2
    end
```

## Better, but nodes alpha blended

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    c1-->a2
    subgraph ide1 [one]
    a1-->a2
    end
    
    style ide1 fill: lightyellow
```

## Uniform styling

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    c1-->a2
    subgraph ide1 [one]
    a1-->a2
    end
    
    style c1 fill: lightgray
    style a1 fill: lightgray
    style a2 fill: lightgray
    style ide1 fill: lightyellow
```

````

Another solution using mermaid theme:

````quarto
---
format: 
  html:
    mermaid: 
      theme: neutral
---

## Legible...

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    c1-->a2
    subgraph ide1 [one]
    a1-->a2
    end
```
````

### Expected behavior

Legible flow chart

### Actual behavior

Subgraph background too dark

title: Improve error messages surrounding notebooks
description:
### Discussed in https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/8920
Originally posted by **nickvigilante** February 28, 2024 ### Description This isn't so much a bug but a request to improve the error messages surrounding notebooks. The common thread between the two issues is to make it easier to identify the file (and the line in the file) that causes issues when running `quarto preview` or `quarto render`. ## Issue 1 I'm new to Jupyter notebooks and Quarto in general, so I thought I'd be able to get away with running `touch notebook.ipynb` to create a new notebook that I know I'll need to write later. I recognize that running `touch notebook.ipynb && jupyter execute notebook.ipynb` throws an error, and now I know I can't create notebooks using `touch`. Despite that, here's what I get when running `quarto preview`: ``` (miniconda3)➜ empty-notebook quarto preview Preparing to preview ERROR: SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input Stack trace: at JSON.parse () at Object.target (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:38264:27) at fileExecutionEngineAndTarget (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:41258:33) at renderContexts (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:72183:38) at Object.renderFormats (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:72234:28) at file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:73380:91 at withRenderServices (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:72589:12) at readBaseInputIndex (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:73380:27) at inputTargetIndex (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:73368:25) at resolveInputTarget (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:73482:25) (miniconda3)➜ empty-notebook ``` If this one notebook is buried among several other notebook files, it's not clear which one is the problematic notebook just by looking at this error message alone. What might be nice is a message like this: ``` ERROR: SyntaxError: Unable to render 'path/to/notebook.ipynb' Caused by: Unexpected end of JSON output Stack trace: ... ``` That way, I know exactly which notebook is malformed and can take steps to fix it, hopefully speeding up my own troubleshooting. This is also applicable to a case where there might have been an unexplained issue when saving the notebook, or if someone manually edited the notebook JSON. Just giving the user a clue about the file where the issue is happening would be immensely helpful. ## Issue 2 I created a notebook with two cells. The label of the first cell is `test-1`, and the second cell has no label (a forced typo for illustrative purposes). I used the `embed` shortcode to embed the two cells in a document: ``` {{< embed notebook.ipynb#test-1 echo=true >}} {{< embed notebook.ipynb#test-2 echo=true >}} ``` When I run `quarto preview`, I get the following message: ``` (miniconda3)➜ json-issue git:(main) ✗ quarto preview Preparing to preview [1/1] index.qmd ERROR: The cell test-2 does not exist in notebook Stack trace: at file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:69687:23 at Array.map () at notebookMarkdown (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:69684:40) at eventLoopTick (ext:core/01_core.js:183:11) at async replaceNotebookPlaceholders (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:69628:32) at async renderPandoc (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:69987:28) at async Object.onRender (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:77261:36) at async renderFileInternal (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:77238:17) at async renderFiles (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:77062:17) at async renderProject (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:77389:25) (miniconda3)➜ json-issue git:(main) ✗ ``` Here are the things that tripped me up: 1. It took testing and experimentation to recognize that `[1/1] index.qmd` does *not* mean that the document rendered correctly. I didn't assume the error message applied to index.qmd. I had assumed that `[X/Y] path/to/file.qmd` meant that `path/to/file.qmd` had successfully rendered. 2. Because of point 1, seeing "The cell X does not exist in the notebook" was unhelpful, because I'm importing several notebooks, each of which [should] have a cell with label X in the notebook. In this situation, I think the following could benefit others: - An explicit reference to the file where the error exists. - An explicit reference to the _line_ in the file causing the error (which would also imply the notebook that's missing the label). - An explicit reference to the path to the notebook that's missing the label. Something like this: ``` (miniconda3)➜ json-issue git:(main) ✗ quarto preview Preparing to preview [1/1] index.qmd ERROR: Error when rendering path/to/index.qmd: Line 13: {{< embed notebook-1.ipynb#test-2 echo=true >}} Caused by: The cell test-2 does not exist in path/to/notebook-1.ipynb Stack trace: ... ``` Having the above would have made (and will continue to make, if implemented) troubleshooting easier. Thanks for your consideration!

title: "ERROR: TypeError: cell.source.join is not a function" thrown when running `quarto preview` with a notebook
description:

title: [FR] Offer a way to add link using new ipv6 convention
description:
Definely something with Pandoc which HTML escape the characters when parsing the link ```` echo '[test](http://[fd04::123]:8080)' | pandoc -f markdown -t native [ Para [ Link ( "" , [] , [] ) [ Str "test" ] ( "http://%5Bfd04::123%5D:8080" , "" ) ] ] ```` They do escape at reading time with usual URI escaping https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/blob/e4ac26d255ad8748c01301b3319975de39a8f43f/src/Text/Pandoc/URI.hs#L29-L32 Note that JS function also does it ```` > encodeURI('http://[fd04::123]:8080') 'http://%5Bfd04::123%5D:8080' ```` So I think those URL are quite specific, right ? It seems it requires a specific handling for ipv6 following recent [RFC3986](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986) https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/encodeURI#encoding_for_rfc3986 So it definitely need an update to Pandoc to follow ipv6 compliance if possible. but you could also for now do that yourself using Lua filter ````lua -- ipv6.lua Link = function(l) if l.classes:includes("ipv6") then _, i = l.classes:find("ipv6") l.classes:remove(i) l.target = l.target:gsub("%%5B", "[") l.target = l.target:gsub("%%5D", "]") end return l end ```` ````powershell ❯ echo '[test](http://\[fd04::123\]:8080){.ipv6}' | pandoc -f markdown -t native --lua-filter=ipv6.lua [ Para [ Link ( "" , [] , [] ) [ Str "test" ] ( "http://[fd04::123]:8080" , "" ) ] ] ```` ````powershell ❯ echo '[test](http://\[fd04::123\]:8080){.ipv6}' | pandoc -f markdown -t html --lua-filter=ipv6.lua

test

```` Hope it helps _Originally posted by @cderv in https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/9229#discussioncomment-8953991_

title: Single images in long scrollable sildes in reveal.js output have height:0
description:
### Bug description

By default revealjs format has `auto-stretch: true`. According to documentation this means: "For slides with a single top-level image, automatically stretch it to fill the slide", but if slide is `scrollable` and has long text, picture or figure is 'stretched' to 0 height.

If I set `auto-stretch: false`, pictures are visible. Also pictures are visible if there is more than 1 on the same slide.

### Steps to reproduce

1. create file `test.qmd`:

````
---
format:
  revealjs:

title: Multiple entries of Large table in the list of tables for scrbook class, when I use knitr::kable()
description:
### Bug description

I am creating a LaTeX document, with the document class `scrbook`. In this document, I am creating a long table, which would span through multiple pages. If I format the table using knitr::kable() function, it will show multiple entries in the list of tables. But when I remove knitr::kable(), there is only one entry for this table in the list of tables.

### Steps to reproduce

````
---
title: "Long Table"
author: "Maulik Bhatt"
format:
  pdf:
    documentclass: scrbook
    toc: true
    lot: true
    pdf-engine: lualatex
---

## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-dummy
#| tbl-cap: "Long Table Spanning Multiple Pages"

dummy_table |> knitr::kable()

There should be only one entry of the long table in the list of tables

### Actual behavior

title: Adding `tbl-colwidths` as a label at the start of Python code cells no longer sets the column width of Markdown tables
description:
### Bug description

In `v1.3.450` of quarto, Using labels at the top of code cells to specify table attributes such as `tbl-colwidths` allowed for per-table formatting when generating a PDF. However, the latest version of quarto (`v1.4.551`) seems to no longer to adhere to this command, and what results is a table that overruns the margins/boundary of the page that it is rendered on.

### Steps to reproduce

The document below renders a simple table using data from `mt-cars`

````qmd
---
format: pdf
echo: false
---

```{python}
#| tbl-colwidths: [20,10,15,10,15,15,15,15,15,15,15,10]

import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown
from tabulate import tabulate

df = pd.read_csv('https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ZeccaLehn/4e06d2575eb9589dbe8c365d61cb056c/raw/64f1660f38ef523b2a1a13be77b002b98665cdfe/mtcars.csv')

df.columns = [
    "Car Name",
    "Fuel Cons. (mpg)",
    "# Cylinders",
    "Displ. (cu.in.)",
    "Gross HP",
    "Rear axle ratio",
    "Weight (1000 lbs)",
    "1/4 mile time",
    "Engine",
    "Trans.",
    "# forward gears",
    "# carburetors",
]

Markdown(
    tabulate(
        df,
        headers="keys",
        showindex=False,
    )
)
```
````

To run, you'll need to copy the above contents into a `.qmd` file, and ensure the Python packages below have been installed. The command I use to render is `quarto render <DOCUMENT_NAME.qmd>`

The packages required to render this document as a pdf are as follows:

```
jupyter==1.0.0
pandas==2.2.1
ipython==8.22.2
tabulate==0.9.0
```



### Expected behavior

A table that has been given `tbl-colwidths` arguments should remain within the margins of the page, with multi-line/wrapped headers based on the specified width of its respective column. See the following output below:

![Screenshot 2024-03-26 144725](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/assets/150830409/899c4631-ce58-4a69-854c-7accd02d918b)


### Actual behavior

In the case of `quarto: v1.4.551`, there is no formatting applied to the columns of the table, and so the result is a table that spills outside of the page right margin:
![Screenshot 2024-03-26 145255](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/assets/150830409/6a1eb5c0-4a4b-423b-8b31-8eaaa7a655b6)

title: Unwanted spacing with revealjs, `echo: true` and `output-location: column`
description:
I think that something weird is happening when using revealjs, `echo: true` and `output-location: column`.

Basically, when the first code chunk appears before the first line of text, one has the "standard" spacing for the chunk of code following the line of text. But when there is no code chunk BEFORE the first line of text, some additional spacing is added between the text and the echoed code. Note that this only happens when using `output-location: column`.

Any idea what might be going on and/or how to solve this?

See below for an MWE with screenshots:
````markdown
---
title: "Test"
format:
  revealjs:
    echo: true
jupyter: python3
---


## Before/after with `output-location: column`

```{python}
#| output-location: column
l = ["a", "b", "c"]; print(l)
```

Code chunks before and after the text

```{python}
#| output-location: column
l = ["a", "b", "c"]; print(l)
```

## After with `output-location: column`

Code chunk only after the text

```{python}
#| output-location: column
l = ["a", "b", "c"]; print(l)
```

## After without `output-location: column`

Code chunk only after the text

```{python}
l = ["a", "b", "c"]; print(l)
```

title: FR: Content selectors for websites
description:
Documentation sites have frequent need to show different content based on user preference / input. Examples:
- Language selectors such as Quarto's main page "Hello, Quarto" section for choosing between Python, R, Julia, or Obserable
- Desired workflow, such as Command Line vs. API
- Documentation version (perhaps related to (https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/474)
- Role, region, or other characteristic

Quarto's support for selectively displaying content is currently limited to panel tabsets, which is not visually appropriate for modifying the content of an entire page. 

A Quarto-native content selector would give users the ability to customize the page (or site) based on their preference or need. 

(ref internal threads [1](https://positpbc.slack.com/archives/C01LQETLA7L/p1709648760879729) and [2](https://positpbc.slack.com/archives/C01LQETLA7L/p1711156979945219))

title: Bibliography can be generated by commented out div
description:
### Bug description

A commented out bibliograpy div like the one below, still causes the bibliography to be created on that particular chapter/page for quarto books.

```
<!-- ## References

::: {#refs}
::: -->
```

I initially didn't realize that a quarto book could only have a single bibliography. When I noticed my second chapter didn't show the bibliography and reading through the documentation, I commented out the divs in both chapters and added an (unnumbered) reference chapter with just the #refs div. However, the bibliography kept showing up in the 1st chapter, and then moved to the 2nd one after I tried removing the entire 1st chapter (thinking it was some kind of weird caching issue). Eventually I realized that the commented out div sections were the culprit and that they were still triggering the bibliography creation.

I'm using the `strip-comments: true` option, in case that matters.

Incidentally, I had also been playing around with the [section-bibliographies](https://github.com/pandoc-ext/section-bibliographies) extension and couldn't get it to work, but I'm beginning to suspect that the same thing was causing an issue.

### Steps to reproduce

_quarto.yml
```
project:
  type: book

book:
  title: "booktest"
  author: "Norah Jones"
  date: "3/27/2024"
  chapters:
    - index.qmd
    - 1.qmd
    - references.qmd

bibliography: references.bib

format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo
```

1.qmd
```
citation @knuth84

<!-- ## References

::: {#refs}
::: -->
```

references.qmd
```
# References {.unnumbered}

::: {#refs}
:::
```


### Expected behavior

Commented out #refs divs should not generate the bibliography on the respective page of a quarto book project.

### Actual behavior

Commented out #refs divs do generate the bibliography on the respective page of a quarto book project, ignoring any uncommented such divs that appear elsewhere.

OS: Windows 10

description:
### Bug description

When specifying parameters via the CLI (for a document using Jupyter), if no default value is specified, the document will not render. If a single (even unrelated) parameter default is specified then it works which is unexpected behavior.



### Steps to reproduce

For example running the follow results in an error as key1 is not found (get error: `NameError: name 'key1' is not defined`)

CLI command: `quarto render test.qmd -P key1:value2`

`test.qmd`
````
---
title: "Test"

jupyter: python3
---

title: Inconsistent behaviour when inserting citations from Zotero in visual editor (RStudio and VSCode)

There seems to be a bug in the former that isn't there in the latter, so the resulting bib entry doesn't contain all the necessary information. (Additionally, unfortunately the bug seems to exist for _both_ insertion methods when using the visual editor in VSCode) ### Steps to reproduce In Zotero, say you have a citation that is type "Conference Paper", with the following data (importantly, it has a "conference name" as well as the title): > **Title: A probabilistic Earley parser as a psycholinguistic model** > Item Type: Conference Paper > Author: John T. Hale > Date: 2001 > Proceedings Title: Second meeting of the North American chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics > **Conference Name: NAACL** > ... etc more information Then, in RStudio, using the visual editor, there are two ways to add this reference to a document in a quarto project, while automatically importing it to a local references.bib file. 1. type inline like `@hal...` and select auto completed citation, then use the "Citation from Zotero" dialogue box to insert the citation into a local bib file (default name 'references.bib'), or 2. use the **Insert > Citation ...** menu item to insert citation from My Sources > Zotero, and select this citation item, and click "Insert" to add to references.bib. ### Expected behavior The expected behaviour would be for a new citation to be added to the references.bib file, corresponding to this citation, with all the relevant fields populated (and in particular the correct information in the title field and booktitle field). ### Actual behavior ### method 1 doesn't work correctly When using method 1 (inserting a citation by typing "@" and using autocompleted citation), the citation item added to references.bib has a title field populated with the conference name (incorrectly), and no booktitle is added. - title: Improve default text highlighting
description:
A quick observation: arrow, the default (AFAIK) highlight-style in Quarto, typesets several types of syntax elements with the same style. For example, the colour #003B4F is used for all of the Normal, Other, ControlFlow and Keyword types [[1]](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/src/resources/pandoc/highlight-styles/arrow-light.theme). This made me think there was something wrong with the syntax highlighter in Quarto, as it seemed to me at first that some types of syntax were not being detected properly, especially when compared to Pandoc where the default (pygments, I think) shows those elements with different styles.

I hit this in the context of typesetting Fortran code (I was expecting SUBROUTINE and IMPLICIT NONE to be highlighted), but the same seems to be true with important Python keywords (e.g. for, in, or, print). Compare the arrow style with the breeze style, where it is much clearer that those elements have been detected and independently styled.
I am happy to switch to breeze, but would it be better if the default highlighting theme in Quarto demonstrated that it can indeed detect these types of syntax elements and typeset them in different styles?

title: Wrongly escaped latex commands
description:
### Bug description

I'm using the `xparse` LaTeX package and defining this function `\NewDocumentCommand \fullarticle {O{scale=.85,clip=true,pages=-} m m O{} O{}}`. This means that there is one optional command, followed by two mandatory commands, and ending with two optional commands.

When trying to inject these values from my `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
fullarticles: |
    \fullarticle[scale=.7,trim={0mm 5mm 0mm 5mm},pages=-]{fischer2017doctoraldissertationmanual}{manual.pdf}[\href{https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/}{\ccbyncnd}]
    \fullarticle[scale=.7,trim={0mm 5mm 0mm 5mm},pages=1]{fischer2017doctoraldissertationmanual}{manual.pdf}[\copyright{} 2018 University of Skövde. Reprinted, with permission, from]
    \fullarticle[scale=.7,trim={0mm 5mm 0mm 5mm},pages=1]{fischer2017doctoraldissertationmanual}{manual.pdf}[Reprinted from][with permission from University of Skövde.]
```

Through the file `after-body.tex`:
```latex
$if(his-metadata.fullarticles)$
  % Example of including full text articles in the manuscript.
  % It's possible to specify what is written both before the reference and after.
  % \fullarticle[includepdf options]{reference}{pdf-file}[before][after]
  \begin{fullarticles}
  $for(his-metadata.fullarticles)$
    $his-metadata.fullarticles$
  $endfor$
  \end{fullarticles}
$endif$
```

The resulting .tex file looks like this:
```latex
\begin{fullarticles}
      \fullarticle[scale=.7,trim={0mm 5mm 0mm 5mm},pages=-]{fischer2017doctoraldissertationmanual}{manual.pdf}{[}\href{https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/}{\ccbyncnd}{]}
      \fullarticle[scale=.7,trim={0mm 5mm 0mm 5mm},pages=1]{fischer2017doctoraldissertationmanual}{manual.pdf}{[}\copyright{}
      2018 University of Skövde. Reprinted, with permission, from{]}
      \fullarticle[scale=.7,trim={0mm 5mm 0mm 5mm},pages=1]{fischer2017doctoraldissertationmanual}{manual.pdf}{[}Reprinted
      from{]}{[}with permission from University of Skövde.{]}
\end{fullarticles}
```

The problem, I think, stems from the fact that the second set of optional arguments are escaped incorrectly. Maybe due to how it's parsed by pandoc? The `xparse` package allows for definition of methods not supported by regular LaTeX and maybe that's throwing the parser off?

### Steps to reproduce

Please see the [his-template](https://github.com/verbalins/his-template) repository. Clone it and compile with `quarto render -t his-pdf` and the problem should be visible in the `Title-for-this-example-thesis.tex` file.

### Expected behavior

Here's the correct LaTeX withouth the extra escapes.
```latex
\begin{fullarticles}
      \fullarticle[scale=.7,trim={0mm 5mm 0mm 5mm},pages=-]{fischer2017doctoraldissertationmanual}{manual.pdf}[\href{https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/}{\ccbyncnd}]
      \fullarticle[scale=.7,trim={0mm 5mm 0mm 5mm},pages=1]{fischer2017doctoraldissertationmanual}{manual.pdf}[\copyright{} 2018 University of Skövde. Reprinted, with permission, from]
      \fullarticle[scale=.7,trim={0mm 5mm 0mm 5mm},pages=1]{fischer2017doctoraldissertationmanual}{manual.pdf}[Reprinted from][with permission from University of Skövde.]
\end{fullarticles}
```

### Actual behavior

```latex
\begin{fullarticles}
      \fullarticle[scale=.7,trim={0mm 5mm 0mm 5mm},pages=-]{fischer2017doctoraldissertationmanual}{manual.pdf}{[}\href{https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/}{\ccbyncnd}{]}

title: Feature request: variables in ojs chunk options (`!expr` for ojs}
description:
Like @agerlach in https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/3260, I am trying to conditionally run chunks in my Quarto doc.

With R I can do this, using the front matter params and `!expr` in the chunk options (as shown in [Quarto documentation](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/3260)).

### Sample QMD

```
---
format: html
params:
  run: false
---
```

````
```{r}
#| eval: !expr params$run
paste("This isn't supposed to run if `run` is false. `run`= ", params$run)
```
````

And, because `!expr params$run` evaluates to `false`, that chunk doesn't run. Good!

For Observable JS, I can *kind of* do this ... and not sure how much it's working.

I can pass `params$run` to ojs with `ojs_define()`, and use this new variable in the ojs chunk options with `ojs_define()`

````
```{r}
ojs_define(run = params$run)
```
````

and check that ojs does indeed have it

````
```{ojs}
"OJS knows run = " + run
```
````

Prints: `"OJS knows run = false"`

and then test it out in the `eval` chunk option.

````
```{ojs}
//| eval: !expr run

"Will an undefined variable trigger an error?"
run // Try a defined variable (defined as false in YAML)
undefined_variable // Try an undefined variable
```
````

Prints:
`"Will an undefined variable trigger an error?"`
`false`

So, we see that the code _does_ run, but interestingly the undefined variable doesn't cause a runtime error. (The rendered output also frames the cell with ":::{.cell eval=“{”value”:“run”,“tag”:“!expr”}“}" at the start and ":::" at the end.". These can be fairly easily hidden with CSS.)

Whereas, if we run the same chunk with `eval: true` we _do_ get a runtime error.

````
```{ojs}
//| eval: true

"Will an undefined variable trigger an error?"
run // Try a defined variable (defined as false in YAML)
undefined_variable // Try an undefined variable
```
````

Prints:
`"Will an undefined variable trigger an error?"`
`false`
Errors: `undefined_variable is not defined`

**All to say, `!expr` is doing something in the ojs cell, but I'm not sure what, and it would be great to have an actual way to use variables as chunk options.**

description:
### Bug description

I tried combining both [metadata includes](https://quarto.org/docs/projects/quarto-projects.html#metadata-includes) and [project-specific configuration](https://quarto.org/docs/projects/profiles.html#profile-configuration) together, but it seems as though metadata includes only apply to the main `_quarto.yml` file.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the following:
 
```bash
quarto create project website config-include-profile-bug
cd config-include-profile-bug
touch _quarto-production.yml
touch _navbar-production.yml
```

2. Insert the following into both `_quarto-production.yml ` and `_navbar-production.yml`:

```yaml
website:
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Home
      - about.qmd
```

3. Remove lines 6 through 10 from `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Home
      - about.qmd
```

4. Run the following commands:

```bash
quarto preview --profile production
```

You should see links for "Home" and "About" in the navbar.

5. Replace `_quarto-production.yml` with the following:

```yaml
metadata-files:
  - _navbar-production.yml
```

Expected: the navbar should still be displayed.

title: quarto incorrectly moves caption location in latex table environment to below Table
description:
### Bug description

If I include a LaTeX table in my quarto document in LaTeX code, the `caption` object gets moved below the table. 

### Steps to reproduce

````
---
format: pdf
tbl-cap-location: top
keep-tex: true
---
  

\begin{table}
\label{tab-test}

\caption{Test caption.}
\begin{tabular}{lr}
\hline
1 & 2 \\
3 & 4
\hline
\end{tabular}

\end{table}
````

### Expected behavior

Should generate a .tex containing:

\centering{

\begin{tabular}{lr}
\hline
1 & 2 \\
3 & 4
\hline
\end{tabular}

}

\end{table}%
```


### Actual behavior

This generates a .tex containing:

```
\begin{table}

\centering{

\begin{tabular}{lr}
\hline
1 & 2 \\
3 & 4
\hline
\end{tabular}

}

\caption{\label{tab-test}Test caption.}

\end{table}%
```


### Your environment

title: Jupyter kernel hangs when using jupyter-client>=8.0.0
description:
### Bug description

When using jupyter-client>=8.0.0, the python3 kernel hangs. 

I am using a Windows 10 laptop, quarto version 1.2.269 to reproduce this bug, but I believe that this persists in later versions of quarto as well (initially stumbled across this when trying to render via a github action which had installed a later version of quarto). 

Steps to reproduce: 

1. Create a fresh python environment (I am currently using python 3.9)
2. Install requirements from a requirements.txt file:

```
notebook==6.5.2
jupyter_client==8.0.1
```

3. Create any .qmd with python code. Example `test.qmd`:

````
---
title: "test quarto"
format:
  html:
    code-fold: true
jupyter: python3
---

Run at least one python cell.

```{python}
print('Hello, World')
```

````

4. Try to render the file:

`quarto render test.qmd`

Quarto will hang on the line `Starting python3 kernel...`

If you change the jupyter_client version to 7.3.5 in the above requirements.txt file, the file will render. 

Interestingly, if you just try to `pip install jupyter` into a fresh environment, it will also hang, but before it even reaches the the `Starting python3 kernel...` line.

title: '_files' folder not inheriting from output filename set on cli
description:
### Bug description

I'm running quarto 1.2.269 on the command line of centos 7.  My use-case is to use the same R script to generate multiple reports, and I like to avoid self_contained/embed-resources so users can easily access individual plots etc. 

```bash
quarto render '01_heatmaps.rmd'   -o 'binarised_v0.0.1-0-ga74c32d.html' -P assay:"binarised" 
```

In Rmarkdown the '*_files' would inherit the name of the output, so I'd get something like `binarised_v0.0.1-0-ga74c32d_files`, but in quarto I'm getting `01_heatmaps_files` - so if I attempt to iterate through a set of parametrised reports, I'll over-write the dependencies.  In [the documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-basics.html#self-contained) it says that this is the 'default' behaviour, but I can't find any way of over-riding this default.  I don't think I can simply rename the folder, as the links then won't work?  Is there a way of reverting the behaviour so that the dependency folder inherits from the output name. Many thanks.

description:
Test I did based on discussion below: * Clone project https://github.com/dmbates/plotdemo which has a `_freeze` folder and use Julia. * Delete the `docs` folder which is the output to recreate and I don't have Julia setup on my environment. * Rendering locally with `quarto preview` -> Julia is not needed. The freezing works - HTML file is created and I can preview result * Trying to publish using `quarto publish quarto-pub` => **Rendering using Julia is happening** - It errors on my side as not setup. So we have an issue here I believe in our publish workflow. Side note : Trying to publish with `--no-render` fails also ```` quarto publish quarto-pub --no-render ? Publish with account christophe.dervieux@gmail.com (Y/n) » Yes ? Publish with name 'plots-demo-5bc8'? (Y/n) » Yes [>] Creating quarto-pub document ERROR: Output file plotdemo.html does not exist. Or another issue cc @cscheid ### Discussed in https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/4237
Originally posted by **dmbates** February 5, 2023 I have been looking at the way that I currently have a Quarto book with Julia code chunks being rendered to gh-pages. (Book is at https://JuliaMixedModels.github.io/EmbraceUncertainty). If I understand the documents at https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html#freezing-computations correctly then setting `freeze: auto` in `_quarto.yml` and rendering the book will save the output of the code chunks in the `_freeze` directory (which I do have committed in the repository). However, the render and publish step fails because it can't access the kernel. (I am actually experimenting on another, private repository but can pull back the curtains if my description is too vague.) Should this be happening or have I misconfigured the github action? title: Visual Editor Changes Figure Labels
description:
### Bug description

In quarto 1.4, When changing from source to visual editor, in both VSCode and RStudio, if there are multiple `.qmd` files in a project, then the name of the current `.qmd` files is prepended into the `#fig-example` labels for figures.

For a file called `intro.qmd`, `#fig-example` becomes `#intro-fig-example`, which subsequently breaks all in-text references to the figure.

The effect stacks. So I tested it in VScode, which prepended the `intro`, then opened in RStudio and tried the visual editor and it did the same thing, turning the example in to `#intro-intro-fig-example`.

Did not previously occur with quarto 1.3.450 which I had installed prior to testing out the daily build.

### Steps to reproduce

Using the base project from `quarto create-project mybook --type book`, in `intro.qmd` I added two possible figures.

````qmd
# Introduction

This is a book created from markdown and executable code.

See @knuth84 for additional discussion of literate programming.

::: {#fig-example}
![](https://i.imgur.com/gSfYoGT.jpg)

A dogo photo.
:::

![](https://i.imgur.com/gSfYoGT.jpg){#fig-example-2}
````

### Expected behavior

The figure labels should remain unchanged, when moving between visual and source editors.

### Actual behavior

`intro` was prepended on to each of the figure labels, resulting int the below `.qmd` file: 

````qmd
# Introduction

This is a book created from markdown and executable code.

See @knuth84 for additional discussion of literate programming.

::: {#intro-fig-example}
![](https://i.imgur.com/gSfYoGT.jpg)

A dogo photo.
:::

![](https://i.imgur.com/gSfYoGT.jpg){#intro-fig-example-2}

title: Using fig-subcap with pdf document causes latex errors
description:
### Bug description

If a chunk has both the chunck options `label` and `fig-subcap`, an extra `figure` environment is created inside the outer `figure` environment, resulting in `LaTeX Error: Not in outer par mode.` when processed to generate PDF.

Example below.

### Steps to reproduce

````
---
title: "`fig-subcap` test"
format: pdf
execute:
    echo: false
    warning: false
editor: source
---

This chunk is successfully processed:

```{r}
#| label: fig-success
#| fig-cap: 'Caption Here'
plot(1:10)
plot(1:10)
```


However, adding a sub-caption results in `LaTeX Error: Not in outer par mode.`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-failure
#| fig-cap: 'Caption Here'
#| fig-subcap: 
#|  - 'Sub-caption 1 Here'
#|  - 'Sub-caption 2 Here'
plot(1:10)
plot(1:10)
```

Removing either the `label` *or* `fig-subcap` chunk option resolves the issue.

````


The error arises because an extra nested `figure` environment is created:

```latex

title: Clean up Shiny docs (R and Python)
description:
[Shiny for Python](https://quarto.org/docs/dashboards/interactivity/shiny-python/) docs currently live under Guide > Dashboards > Interactivity > Shiny for Python

[Shiny for R](https://quarto.org/docs/interactive/shiny/) docs mostly live under Guide > Interactivity > Shiny (i.e. not under Dashboards, although some pages are included in both locations Guide > Dashboards, and Guide > Interactivity).

This currently leads to confusion:

* Navigating to Guide > Interactivity > Shiny > Running Documents, drops you into the Dashboard docs
* Shiny for Python isn't mentioned in Guide > Interactivity 

Some questions to consider:

* How do "Guide > Interactivity" and "Guide > Dashboards > Interactivity" differ? Do we need both? What content can be shared? How should they be linked? What distinctions do we want to outline for users?

* Do we still need Component Layout https://quarto.org/docs/interactive/layout.html ?  I think this page should focus on the layout of components in longer form articles, and link to dashboards for full page layouts.

* Where do we talk about the difference between a Quarto dashboard with Shiny Python, and a Shiny Python app (ditto for R): no `server()` function, no ui layout functions e.g. `ui.page_fluid()` etc, no call to `App()`, no `@output` decorator (python), adding `#| context: server` (R)? Some mentions in various places, but it would be nice to have some side by side comparisons of code.

title: Quarto presentation render fails on second try after deleting cache when using `cache` with `leaflet::addProviderTiles`
description:
### Bug description

**Note:** I [reported this](https://community.rstudio.com/t/quarto-presentation-render-fails-on-second-try-after-deleting-cache-when-using-cache-with-leaflet-addprovidertiles/158757) over at community.rstudio.com, but I suppose that this is a better place for it.

I am using RStudio 2022.12.0 Build 353 with R version 4.2.2 Patched (2022-11-10 r83330) and knitr-1.41 on a Ubuntu  20.04.5 LTS installation.

I have identified a problem using `cache: true` in a quarto document that uses the `leaflet` package, specifically when using `addProviderTiles`. An example document that demonstrates the problem is below:

````
---
title: "test"
format: revealjs
---

## Create some random spatial data

```{r}
library(sf)
library(leaflet)

# List of volcanos -----------------------------------------
v = c("Volcán Villarica, Chile","Volcán Lonquimay, Chile")

lon = c("Volcán Villarica, Chile"=-71.93,
        "Volcán Lonquimay, Chile"=-71.58)
lon = lon[v]

lat = c("Volcán Villarica, Chile"=-39.42,
        "Volcán Lonquimay, Chile"=-38.38)
lat = lat[v]

volcanoes = data.frame(name=v,lon=lon,lat=lat)
volcanoes = st_as_sf(volcanoes,coords=c("lon","lat"),crs=4326)

lf = volcanoes |> leaflet() |> addTiles() |> addMarkers()
```

## This works with cache

```{r}
#| cache: true
lf
```

## This fails with cache on second render

```{r}
#| cache: true
lf |> addProviderTiles(providers$OpenTopoMap)
```
````

 The document renders without problem the first time before the `cache` exists, but the second time it fails with the following error about missing dependencies:

```
Error: path for html_dependency not found: /tmp/RtmpXpw2HT
Execution halted
```

Deleting the cache allows it to render again, but one looses the `cache` functionality.

description:
### Bug description

Some RevealJS themes (beige, league, sky) don't support animation of code line number highlighting per https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/#line-highlighting (see the example where one can advance with space-bar to show highlighted lines). In the faulty themes, it seems the "background" code is not properly grayed out (so the highlighted code appears to stand out).

Here's a MWE for the problem:

````md
---
format: 
    revealjs: 
        theme: beige # doesn't work
        # theme: blood # works
        # theme: dark # works
        # theme: default # works
        # theme: league # doesn't work
        # theme: moon # works
        # theme: night # works
        # theme: serif # works
        # theme: simple # works
        # theme: sky # doesn't work
        # theme: solarized # works
---

# Animated slide

```{.python code-line-numbers="|6|9"}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

r = np.arange(0, 2, 0.01)

ax.set_rticks([0.5, 1, 1.5, 2])

title: Caption not showing when using inline SVG in Figure AST node
description:
This is to track possible enhancement/fix when inline HTML such as SVG is included in a Figure Pandoc AST node (such as the one emitted by `diagram.lua` below). Note that the issue was raised in the discussion below when using a version of under active development. A workaround has been found and is documented in the discussion. ### Discussed in https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/5266
Originally posted by **netw0rkf10w** April 21, 2023 Hello, I'm using [this filter](https://github.com/pandoc-ext/diagram/blob/main/diagram.lua) for converting TikZ code to SVG in Quarto. When using the filter as is, it works (an example can be found at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pandoc-ext/diagram/main/test/input-tikz.md). However, when I changed the code to replace the SVG file with inline SVG, the caption is not showing (I checked the output HTML and the `figure` container was not even generated). More precisely, in the original code, an SVG image is created and store in `img`, then: ```lua -- Use the block's filename attribute or create a new name by hashing the image content. local basename, _extension = pandoc.path.split_extension( props.filename or pandoc.sha1(img) ) local fname = basename .. '.' .. extension_for_mimetype[imgtype] -- Store the data in the media bag: pandoc.mediabag.insert(fname, imgtype, img) -- Create a figure that contains just this image. local img_obj = pandoc.Image(props.alt, fname, "", props['image-attr']) return pandoc.Figure(pandoc.Plain{img_obj}, props.caption, props['fig-attr']) ``` What I did is, instead of creating a file in the media bag, I used directly the SVG as an inline HTML element: ```lua return pandoc.Figure(pandoc.RawInline('html', img), props.caption, props['fig-attr']) ``` (the above line replaces the entire previous code block) **Using Pandoc alone, it worked:** ``` quarto pandoc --lua-filter filters/diagram.lua -s tikz.qmd -o tikz.html ``` However, when rendering `tikz.qmd` containing ``` filters: - diagram.lua ``` with Quarto, the SVG is displayed but not in a figure container and thus there's no caption. Could you please help? Thank you very much in advance!

title: Handle better xelatex missing on non TinyTeX installation
description:
From: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/7676, TinyTeX is not available on ARM so Quarto can sometimes be used with OS package manager texlive. 

As shared

````sh
sudo apt-get update

We should try detect that and advice

description:

I would like to pass arguments to the deno engine, because I recieve a js error when rendering a document:

    at async renderFiles (file:///C:/Program%20Files/Quarto/bin/quarto.js:86593:51)
```

This error can be resolved by increasing v8 engine's stack size: [see SO](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76497555/quarto-julia-stack-size-exceeded-error-on-macos).
On a **Linux** system I am able to pass arguments by setting the following environment variable:
```bash
export QUARTO_DENO_EXTRA_OPTIONS=--v8-flags=--stack-size=10000
```

On a **Windows** system, however, the options defined in this variable do not get passed to deno (see below).

### Steps to reproduce

Try to render any document to html with setting the `QUARTO_DENO_EXTRA_OPTIONS` environment variable:

```powershell
PS> $Env:QUARTO_DENO_EXTRA_OPTIONS = "--v8-flags=--invalid-argument"
PS> quarto render .\quarto_bug.qmd
```
Example `quarto_bug.qmd` file:

````
---
format: html
---

```{python}
print('Hello world')
```
````

### Expected behavior

The `deno` engine should raise an error if it sees the argument:
```powershell 
PS> ./deno run --v8-flags="--invalid-argument" -
error: V8 did not recognize flag '--invalid-argument'

For a list of V8 flags, use '--v8-flags=--help'
```

Under a Linux system (WSL) this is exactly what happens:
```bash
$ export $QUARTO_DENO_EXTRA_OPTIONS="--v8-flags=--invalid-argument"
$ quarto render quarto_bug.qmd --to html
error: V8 did not recognize flag '--invalid-argument'

For a list of V8 flags, use '--v8-flags=--help'
```

### Actual behavior

On Windows the document is rendered without deno crashing (which means the options were not passed).  Probably the content of the environment variable is overwritten inside Quarto.

title: RHEL build is failing from v1.5.22
description:
Just to track the problem as resolution depends on external tooling. 

* Our RHEL build is now failing: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/actions/runs/8106380665/job/22156220551
* This is following latest Deno upgrade to v1.41.0: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/pull/8907 because 
	*  The RHEL build requires conda-forge deps
		https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/ad16f0661d9d576c71f715f048f0c9bfca3947db/.github/workflows/create-release.yml#L192-L201
	* deno 1.41.0 is not yet on conda-forge: https://github.com/conda-forge/deno-feedstock/pull/93. There is a failure there to fix. Not straightforward. 

As we don't know when upstream will be fixed, we need to make the build optional for the future pre-release, and let us time until the next 1.5 official release to fix it. 

Until this is solved, all the future 1.5 pre-releases ~and 1.4 patch releases~ won't have the rhel bundle included. **This could be breaking change for anyone user which has scripted around downloading rhel artifact when we do a new release**. 

Todo, while we take the time to fix this:

- [ ] ~Warn in next 1.4 patch release changelog about this maybe...~ Patch 1.4 has the bundle so all good
- [x] Make the rhel build optional to unblock the release creation process  (PR #8945)

title: Further customisation of cross-ref labels

title: [columns] div tag layout on html page impacts columns layout
description:
### Bug description We are prototyping a tool to compile several reveal.js presentation into a single html file with a colleague of mine. The workflow implies to read html code with `rvest::read_html()` to post process the html files. When including columns in one of our test presentations. We noticed that the column was not rendered as expected. It turns out that `rvest::read_html()` lints the code and automatically escape a line after each closing tag. I would expect that style change not to affect the behaviour of the page but unfortunately it does. When escaping a line after a div tag of class "column" `
`, the result of the two columns is displayed one on top of the other instead of side by side. ### Steps to reproduce Here is a working qmd reprex. ``` qmd --- title: "Quarto colums" --- # Columns :::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} A ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} B ::: :::: ``` When rendering it we obtained the normal layout, column contents are displayed side-by-side. ![image](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/assets/43757522/8cb80946-69d6-42e5-bcbc-070dadd88226) The underlying html code looks like this ```html

Columns

A

B

``` Now if we (or our pipeline) escape a line after the closing div tag of the first column ```html

Columns

A

B

``` This causes the column content to be rendered one on top of the other. ![image](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/assets/43757522/40c96917-34af-43b5-bd07-3f6d1fe679c2) ### Expected behavior I will expect that the position of the div tag relative to each other won't impact the rendered layout. Adding an extra line break should not modify the rendered layout. ```html

Columns

A

B

``` ![image](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/assets/43757522/8cb80946-69d6-42e5-bcbc-070dadd88226) ### Actual behavior Introducing an additional line break in the html code modifies the layout. The content of the column is rendered vertically instead of horizontally. ```html

Columns

A

B

title: Impossible to preview docusaurus website
description:
### Bug description

Hello !

I am trying to migrate to the latest version of quarto, while doing this migration I discovered it is impossible for me to preview my docusaurus website with the command `quarto preview`.

After some debug, I found it is because I have a `_quarto.yml` to define configurations at project level.
If I remove it, it is working good. It seems quarto got difficulty to parse this file.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a basic docusaurus website
2. Add the following `_quarto.yml` file

```yml
project:
  type: docusaurus

format:
  docusaurus-md:
    code-fold: true

execute:
  warning: false
```
3. Run the command `quarto preview`

### Expected behavior

Project preview should be supported for docusaurus project.

### Actual behavior

It crashs with the following error.

description:
### Bug description

I am unsure whether this would be even the expected behaviour, so feel free to flag it as not. 

I am generating documentation for a website. I have a `.qmd` file that is generated from a pre-render script that generates the file. As the file initially doesn't exist, quarto ignores it even if I explicitly list it in the `contents`.

When it is then run a second time, it will then include it. Even though it is regenerated, because it was there initially it picks it up and renders the newly generated one.

### Steps to reproduce

A reproducible example is these three files:

`_quarto.yml`
```yml
project:
  type: website
  output-dir: _build
  pre-render: script.py

website:
  title: "Test"
  sidebar:
    contents:
      - index.qmd
      - script.qmd
```
`index.qmd`
```md
# Testing!

This is some text.

Lots of text goes in here.
```

`script.py`
```python
with open("script.qmd", "w") as file:
    file.write('# This is generated\n')
    file.write('By a python script, none the less!')

That the generated `.qmd` file would be included as it is listed directly in the `_quarto.yml`.

title: Whitespace problems with markdown parsing.
description:
### Bug description

Parsing of the markdown seems to be dependent on whitespace on ways that are not documented.

1) When using `$` delimiters for LaTeX equations, if there is whitespace between the delimiter and the equation, quarto quotes the delimiters instead of rendering the equation.  

2) When using bulleted lists, if there is not a blank line between the end of the paragraph and the start of the list, then the bullet characters are quoted and the list is run into the paragraph.

This happens both when rendering in Quarto and when switching back and forth between the R Studio source and visual modes.

These restrictions on syntax do not appear to be documented (certainly not in the quick help from RStudio).

### Steps to reproduce

```qmd
---
title: "Syntax Issues"
---

Putting whitespace between the dollar sign and the equation produces problems.

This works $H \rightarrow E$

But this does not $ H \rightarrow E $

Not leaving a blank line before the item causes a problem. 
* Item 1 
* Item 2

But if I leave a blank line it works.

*  Item 1
*  Item 2

```
This renders as follows:

[syntaxIssues.pdf](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/files/12524936/syntaxIssues.pdf)


### Expected behavior

I expect both examples in both cases to be the same:

1) I expect the equation to be rendered twice.

2) I expect both lists to look the same.

### Actual behavior

With extra whitespace, the equation does not render.  Switching from source->visual->source in R studio changes the equation to `\$ H \rightarrow \$`.

Without the blank line, the list is run into the same paragraph.  Switching from source->visual->source produces

```qmd
Not leaving a blank line before the item causes a problem.  \* Item 1 \* Item 2
```

title: Document unsupported knitr chunk options
description:
Where should we set knitr chunk options in YAML? The original proposal from Max was:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    fig-width: 6
    fig-height: 4.25
    fig-align: center
```

or

```
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    fig-width: 6
    fig-height: 4.25
    fig-align: center
```

More comments from him:

> Any recommendation? Are there certain options that should go in one place or another?

> Also, I have the equivalent of _common.R. I’d like to specific device settings there using `knitr::opts_chunk$set(blah blah blah)`
> Does that work too? I’d use this to alter options based on the target format (i.e. HTML versus LaTeX). 

> It looks like dev shouldn't be set in _quarto.yml (and is silently ignored). I set dev: svg for HTML format and it tried to use png.

> My understanding is that some of them can be set under execute in the YAML: https://quarto.org/docs/reference/formats/html.html#execution.

> And some under knitr: https://quarto.org/docs/reference/cells/cells-knitr.html

> And I think instead of dev it's fig-format?
> I'm also curious about the "right" answer to this.
> And I'm fairly certain you can use  `knitr::opts_chunk$set(blah blah blah)`.

I (@allenmanning) answered:

> you can use the R code version. also yes its fig-format. The format: html is for universally supported quarto options (i.e. stuff that works in jupyter and knitr). we've attempted to support as much as possible in both but knitr still has a lot of things that jupyter doesn't (thus the opts_chunk failsafe). So I'd say that the correct/recommended approach is to use the universal options (fig-format, execute: echo, etc.) and then only use the opts_chunk for things that are unsupported with the normal syntax

Is there a list of the unsupported options?

we don't currently

title: Document inline conditional content
description:
The documentation for [conditional content](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/conditional.html) only discusses the use of divs, but you can also use inline CSS for conditional content. It would be nice if this was documented on the conditional content page too.

Here's a reprex .qmd for demonstration:

```qmd
---
title: "Reprex"
format:
  pdf: default
  html: default
---

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}

Will only appear in HTML. (div)

:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}

Will only appear in PDF. (div)

:::

[Will only appear in HTML. (inline)]{.content-visible when-format="html"}

[Will only appear in PDF. (inline)]{.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
```

title: Add --title option back for quarto create project
description:
Previous versions of quarto allowed commands like:

> quarto create-project --type website --title "My Website"

It was nice that the location of the files (in this case, the current directory) and the title of the project could be different. That is no longer possible in version 1.4. Best you can do is:

> quarto create project website .

This, hackily, puts everything in the current directory. But then it also gives the project a title of ".". That is not what anyone wants!

Best solution would be to allow back the --title option.

title: Resource Path Issue
description:
### Bug description

Rendering to PDF with a specified resource path doesn't appear to work as expected. I am specifying an image directory but I receive an error saying that the images cannot be located.

Quarto documentation referring to resource path parameter: https://quarto.org/docs/reference/formats/pdf.html#rendering

### Steps to reproduce

Here is a small demo I created and zipped up:

[quarto-cli-resource-path-issue.zip](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/files/13218507/quarto-cli-resource-path-issue.zip)

It contains a `document.md`, `images`, and `README.md`.

In here I am trying to render `document.md` as a PDF by running:

```bash
quarto render document.md --to pdf --resource-path=./images
```

The following error is returned:

```bash
compilation failed- error
Unable to load picture or PDF file 'radiator.jpg'.
<to be read again> 
                   }
l.172 }
```

Note that resource path works with pandoc

```bash
pandoc document.md --to pdf -o document.pdf --resource-path=./images
```


### Expected behavior

title: Julia plots not respecting embed-resources
description:
### Bug description

The [html documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/reference/formats/html.html) states that `embed-resources` can be used to create a standalone html that should inline figures created from execution blocks through a data URI. Apologies if I missed something in the documentation, but I assume that setting this to false would save any figures as external files in the default  `<document>_files` directory with a src link in an img tag in the html output.

This works when creating a figure with R or python + matplotlib; however, when running Julia through Jupyter, plots are embedded as base64 strings in the html output even when `embed-resources` is set to false. Note, issue persists even in the latest quarto pre-release.

### Steps to reproduce

---
title: "Test document"
execute:
    fig-format: png
format:
    html:
        embed-resources: false
---

R plot

```{R}
plot(1:10, 1:10)
```

title: "Test document"
jupyter: julia-1.10

format:

using Plots

plot(1:10, 1:10)

### Expected behavior

In both cases the figures should be saved as external files and linked in the html output through a `src` attribute.

Hello,

I encountered an issue trying to layout sub-figures in Quarto's new manuscript project type. I don't know if this extends to other formats as I don't have much time to test, I'm using the format for work.

- When using `column: page` in the chunk options, the layout applies to each subfigure, and they end up on top of each other.

- When switching to two `fig-cap:` options, the figures are positioned correctly, but I lose the possibility of having a common caption along with subcaptions.

- Enclosing the code chunk in a div with only `{.column-page}` to get the best out of divs and chunks works in HTML, but crashes in LaTeX PDF render as Quarto tries to fit a float in a box. 

I'll put the steps to reproduce each output. I reproduced this in the `index.qmd` file of the [Quarto manuscript template](https://github.com/quarto-ext/manuscript-template-rstudio).   geom_point()) |> ggplotly()

(iris |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width)) +
  geom_point()) |> ggplotly()
```
````

This chunk was expected to produce two side by side sub-figures spanning the page, but it produced two stacked sub-figures, each spanning the entire page width. This chunk renders well in LaTeX, producing two side-by-side figures.

```
:::
````

This yields the correct layout in HTML, but crashes during LaTeX render.

### Expected behavior

I wanted **Chunk 1** to render correctly in HTML and PDF, yielding this figure:

![fig-subcap-ok](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/assets/125131068/267a79cc-3b87-4530-9513-a952a499685f)

title: Website sidebar auto generation fails for new files created by pre-render script
description:
### Bug description

With the following setup,

`index.qmd`:
```
Example Website
```

`create.sh`:
```
#!/bin/sh
mkdir -p example
echo "hello" > example/hello.qmd
```

`_quarto.yml`:
```
project:
  type: website
  pre-render: sh create.sh

website:
  title: Example Website
  sidebar:
    title: "Example Sidebar"
    contents:
      - index.qmd
      - auto: "example"
```

I see the following error when running `QUARTO_PRINT_STACK=true quarto render`,

```
ERROR: TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object

TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object
    at Function.keys (<anonymous>)
    at findIndexFile (file:///Applications/quarto/bin/quarto.js:91210:19)

title: v2 Google Fonts API?
description:
It looks like the embedded [bootswatch themes ](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/tree/main/src/resources/formats/html/bootstrap/themes) currently use the v1 Google Fonts API that doesn't support variable fonts:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/a14f4b3090178f8e01f17e28a9e93d3f5b269065/src/resources/formats/html/bootstrap/themes/sketchy.scss#L169


It doesn't seem to impact behavior of themes now, but something to be aware of is the v2 Google Fonts API uses a different base URL, see:
https://developers.google.com/fonts/docs/css2

title: Python .qmd render deletes existing same-name notebook
description:
### Problem Description

I am most comfortable in Python, and commonly run analyses in `.ipynb` files. 

Several times I have started an analysis in a jupyter notebook, before migrating to a `.qmd` file for the finalized report. In these cases my original notebook would be named something like `analysis.ipynb` and I create a new file called `analysis.qmd`. Then when I go to preview the qmd file, quarto generates a _new_ `analysis.ipynb` file that overwrites all the existing work inside the original notebook, and then deletes the notebook

### Proposed Change
Quarto should not create new files with the same file path as already existing files within the working directory. In the case of the jupyter notebooks used for rendering a randomized uuid or number can be attached to the filename to ensure user code is not irrecoverably deleted.

title: Some engine combinations trigger unexpected tlmgr updates
description:
### Bug description

Using

```
-M pdf-engine:latexmk -M pdf-engine-opt:-outdir=/tmp/out
```

without first disabling the built-in engine with `latex-auto-mk: false` triggers:

```
Rendering PDF
running latexmk - 1
  Rc files read:
    NONE
  Latexmk: Nothing to do for 'test.tex'.
  
  
updating tlmgr

updating existing packages
```

I admit this is a weird combination of options, but a quite similar one is given [in the documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/pdf-engine.html#alternate-pdf-engines):

> pdf-engine: lualatex
> pdf-engine-opt: -outdir=out

So perhaps this should be clarified in the documentation, rejected from the command line or made to work somehow. 

### Steps to reproduce

For a dummy test.qmd document run:

```
quarto render test.qmd -t pdf -M pdf-engine:latexmk -M pdf-engine-opt:-outdir=/tmp/out
```

Then try it again disabling the built-in builder:

```
quarto render test.qmd -t pdf -M latex-auto-mk:false -M pdf-engine:latexmk \
    -M pdf-engine-opt:-outdir=/tmp/out
```

### Expected behavior

If this is not expected to work, clarify it in the documentation and rejected the combination from the CLI. Otherwise make it work properly. It shouldn't start any updating process.

Shown above.

title: No hyphenation for lang: es
description: ### Bug description When using the frontmatter: ``` --- lang: es --- ``` I expect a pdf rendered using latex to have proper Spanish indentation (or any indentation whatsoever) as described in https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/language.html. From which I infer the proper behavior would have been to install the required packages when `lang: es` or to provide them preinstalled in tinytex. Instead, I had to manually install hyphen-spanish using tlmgr. ### Steps to reproduce prueba.qmd ``` --- lang: es --- automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente automáticamente ``` ``` quarto uninstall tinytex quarto install tinytext quarto render prueba.qmd -t pdf ``` ``` tlmgr update --self tlmgr install hyphen-spanish quarto render prueba.qmd -t pdf ``` ### Expected behavior The documented behavior: everything is properly autoinstalled so then hyphenation works for the document's language. ### Actual behavior No hyphenation for Spanish. ### Your environment macOS Sonoma ### Quarto check output ``` Quarto 1.4.549 [✓] Checking versions of quarto binary dependencies...
